docs.title: pipeloom
docs.text:
Engine-agnostic data pipelines: Python models marked with @model, YAML for the project.

pipeloom discovers the @model functions of a project, checks it in layers, builds the dependency graph, writes the execution plan as a manifest and runs it on polars, pandas or Spark, with incremental models, merge, partition and scd2 writes, contracts, data-quality expectations, unit and data tests, retries, timeouts and cancellation.

  • Quickstart
  • Guides: running a pipeline, incremental models, write strategies, data quality, retries and cancellation
  • Reference: command line, JSON Schema, run artifacts, error codes
  • Architecture
  • Architecture decision records
Where to start, by role. Source: use-cases.d2.

docs.title: pipeloom architecture
docs.text: Status: the code implements the versions listed in section 16: the scheduler, the polars, pandas and Spark engines, incremental models, merge, replace_partitions and scd2, expectations and quarantine, retries, timeouts and cancellation, the Databricks and Airflow integrations, per-model catalogs and, from 0.9, Python-first authoring. 1.0 freezes the contracts: what stays stable within a major version is listed in Stability and deprecations. Planned work lives in the roadmap. Decisions are recorded as ADRs in adr/. Diagrams are D2 sources in docs/diagrams with committed light and dark SVGs. From 0.9 models are decorated Python functions, and YAML keeps the project and properties files (ADR-0050). Through 0.8 every model was declared in a YAML model file (ADR-0003, superseded); that path is removed, and Migrating from 0.8 maps it to the decorator.

docs.title: 1. Vision, goals, non-goals, principles
docs.text:
Vision. A small, typed framework. Models are written in Python and the project and properties in YAML (from 0.9; through 0.8 pipelines are declared in YAML), then compiled into an immutable plan. That plan runs the same way on pandas, polars, PySpark or later engines, and runs locally, as one Databricks job, or as an Airflow DAG. Every run produces a single event stream and artifacts you can query.

Goals: Python models with a typed decorator, and YAML project and properties files with layered validation and editor completion; an engine-agnostic core with one plugin per tool; end-to-end events and styled logs; persisted metadata for each run and each model; a Databricks one-job renderer; a cosmos-style Airflow integration; open-source hygiene.

Non-goals (through 1.0, replaced after 1.0 by the list below): streaming; a scheduler service, or any UI that starts, schedules or changes runs (ADR-0043); a portable SQL dialect; Jinja templating; running user code at compile time (from 0.9: user code runs at compile time only for modules with dynamic decorator arguments, ADR-0050); Airflow 2 support.

Non-goals (after 1.0, ADR-0016 amendment 1.1 and the roadmap): streaming (reading Auto Loader or Lakeflow Connect landing tables through incremental is supported, checkpoint-based state is not); a scheduler service, or any UI or agent tool that starts, schedules or changes runs (MCP write tools fall under it); a portable SQL dialect; Jinja templating; user code at compile time beyond ADR-0050; Airflow 2 support; zero-copy environments (clone-only dev copies are allowed, promotion is not); a semantic layer; cross-engine data diff; ML anomaly models beyond fixed statistics. Engines beyond polars, pandas, Spark and DuckDB are community plugins tested by the conformance kit.

Principles. Each answers a lesson (L) from the concept spec. 1. One event stream. Logs, metrics, artifacts and lineage subscribe to it (L1). 2. Dependencies are declared, never traced. Tracing is an opt-in static check that warns (L2). 3. No module-level registries. A Project object owns plugins and config (L3). 4. Docs, the CLI reference, the JSON Schema and the error catalog are all generated from code. Every CLI flag has a test (L4). 5. No session-global mutation. Every engine setting lives in a context manager with guaranteed cleanup. Metrics never depend on global commit tags (L5, L10). 6. Ready-queue scheduling with no level barriers (L6). 7. Execution units never share in-memory state. Ephemeral models are inlined; intermediates are persisted (L7). 8. Maintenance operations (compaction, clustering) run only when declared (L8). 9. Each declared write option is either applied by every strategy or rejected at validation (L9). 10. Platform behavior is injected: clock, identity, catalog, secrets (L11). 11. Incremental logic is a declared key plus a lookback, with a watermark store (L12). 12. Retries, timeouts, data quality, persisted metadata, selectors, schema-change policy, SCD2 and deletes are all first-class (L13). 13. Python-first models, YAML with JSON Schema for the project and properties (L14; from 0.9, ADR-0050; through 0.8 YAML first).

docs.title: 2. Glossary
docs.text:
• Project: a directory with pipeloom.yml, Python model modules and properties YAML files (through 0.8: YAML model files).
  • Model: a named dataset built from declared inputs. From 0.9 it is a Python function marked with @model, whose parameters are its inputs; through 0.8 it is a YAML entry with a Python callable or a SQL body.
  • Source: an external dataset declared in YAML. From 0.9 sources are tables in named groups under sources: in pipeloom.yml, with the unique id source.<project>.<group>.<table>.
  • Properties file: (from 0.9) any *.yml or *.yaml under model_paths other than pipeloom.yml; it describes and configures models by name and never declares one.
  • Folder config: (from 0.9) the models: tree of pipeloom.yml, whose +key settings apply to the models of a folder and its subfolders.
  • Target: a named runtime environment (engine, catalog, naming, state store).
  • Materialization: table, incremental, view, ephemeral or intermediate.
  • Write strategy: append, overwrite, replace_partitions, merge or scd2.
  • Plan: an immutable compiled graph of resolved models.
  • Execution unit: one schedulable node of the plan. It holds one persisted model plus any ephemeral models inlined into it.
  • Boundary: process (all units in one process) or task (each unit in its own process or orchestrator task).
  • Manifest: the serialized plan (manifest.json).
  • Run: one execution of a plan, identified by run_id.
  • Invocation: one process taking part in a run.
  • Attempt: one try of a unit.
  • Watermark: the high-water value of an incremental key.
  • Expectation: a data-quality rule with warn, drop or fail.
  • Sink: an event subscriber.
  • Renderer: turns a plan into an orchestrator artifact.
  • Executor: runs units.
  • Plugin API version: the version of the protocol contract between the core and plugins.

docs.title: 3. Architecture overview
docs.text:
pipeloom in context. Source: context.d2.

Layers. Arrows point toward dependencies. The core never imports a plugin, and an import-linter contract enforces this in CI.

CLI / Python API (pipeloom.api.Project)
  ├─ diagnostics  Diagnostic, Report, Outcome and the error-code catalog (`pipeloom.diagnostics.codes`); a leaf package
  ├─ platform   Clock and Identity seams
  ├─ authoring  `@model`, `ModelSpec`, `ref`, `source`, `var` and the check helpers (from 0.9)
  ├─ discovery  AST resolver, discovery cache, ModuleLoader, load summary (from 0.9)
  ├─ config     YAML loader with line marks, pydantic models, defaults resolution, target binding, schema export
  ├─ validate   L2 references, L4 plan semantics, L5 capabilities, L6 static code (L0-L1 live in config, L3 in graph)
  ├─ graph      DAG, selectors, topological order, cycle paths
  ├─ plan       Plan, ExecutionUnit, Manifest, plan_hash
  ├─ runtime    Scheduler, Executor(thread|process), ModelRunner, ModelContext
  ├─ engine     protocols, logical types, capabilities, portable helpers (Narwhals)
  ├─ incremental / quality / state
  ├─ events     Event models, EventBus, console/jsonl/file sinks
  ├─ artifacts  manifest.json, run_results.json writers
  ├─ secrets    env provider, interpolation, redaction
  ├─ plugins    entry-point discovery, built-in table, API-version gate
  ├─ builtins   naming strategies, filesystem catalog spec, env secret provider
  └─ testing    contract suites, RecordingSink, FakeClock, MemoryEngine
Plugins: pipeloom-pandas | -polars | -spark (0.4) | -databricks (0.5) | -airflow (0.6) | -openlineage (0.9)

pipeloom-spark depends only on pipeloom. pyspark is not a dependency of it: the extra local brings pyspark[connect] and delta-spark, and pipeloom[spark] pulls pipeloom-spark[local] (ADR-0031). Databricks runtimes and Databricks Connect ship their own pyspark, so there the plugin is installed without extras.

Distributions and their dependencies. The entry-point groups each plugin fills are listed in section 6. Source: packages.d2. Core modules; arrows point at the module imported. Source: core-modules.d2.

Lifecycle. Each stage is a pure function from the previous stage's output. Every stage emits events.

  1. Load: discover YAML files, then parse them while recording file, line and column for every node. From 0.9 the same scan also finds Python model files: an AST pass resolves static @model decorators without importing, the discovery cache skips unchanged files, and an import pass loads only the modules with dynamic decorator arguments (section 4).
  2. Validate schema: pydantic models (L0-L1), over YAML and, from 0.9, over decorator arguments.
  3. Resolve graph: bind refs and sources (from 0.9, function parameters), apply defaults and precedence, apply naming strategies to get physical names, apply selectors (L2-L3). A model's schema goes to the naming strategy; a model's catalog (same cascade as schema: through 0.8 the model file, folder _defaults.yml or defaults.models; from 0.9 the decorator, properties and the models: tree) replaces the catalog of the relation the strategy returns, so naming strategies keep transforming only the schema (ADR-0040). Path catalogs (filesystem, delta_path) lay a table out at <root>/<catalog>/<schema>/<name>/ when the relation has a catalog; catalogs with a catalog level (spark_catalog, unity) never create the catalog, only the schema.
  4. Validate plan: semantics, plugin capabilities and static code checks (L4-L6).
  5. Compile: fuse ephemeral models into units for the chosen boundary, then freeze. Output is Plan plus manifest.json with a plan_hash (sha256 of the canonical JSON of nodes, sources, units, edges and the project, target, boundary and config version; selection, versions, timestamps and ids are excluded).
  6. Execute: the scheduler runs units through an executor. Orchestrated tasks run pipeloom run --manifest ... --select unit:<id> --expect-plan-hash <h>.
  7. Finalize: merge per-invocation results, write run_results.json, commit run state, flush and close sinks.

Commands. init (scaffold a new project, ADR-0041), new model (add one decorated .py model file; ADR-0041 amendments), validate, compile, ls, graph (with --units, the unit graph for orchestrators, ADR-0049), run, retry (run again what a finished run did not finish, ADR-0013 amendment), test and build (unit tests, then a run with data tests, ADR-0045), runs ls|show (run history, ADR-0047), finalize, docs generate|serve (a read-only one-file site, ADR-0043), schema export, explain (print a diagnostic code's catalog entry and docs link) and plugins list; plugins add their own through pipeloom.commands (for example pipeloom databricks).

Lifecycle stages and the artifacts they write. Source: lifecycle.d2. Stage Error codes Writes 1. Load PLY (L0) 2. Validate schema PLS (L1) 3. Resolve graph PLR, PLG (L2, L3) 4. Validate plan PLP, PLC, PLK (L4 to L6); PLF with --preflight 5. Compile manifest.json 6. Execute PLX, PLM, PLQ, PLE, PLU units/<unit_id>/attempt-<n>.json 7. Finalize run_results.json, the run record in the state store

docs.title: 4. Configuration
docs.text:
From 0.9 (ADR-0050) a project is one pipeloom.yml, Python model modules and optional properties files. The YAML model files of 0.8 are gone; see "YAML model files" below.

Project file.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://emanuel-luis.github.io/pipeloom/latest/schema/v1/project.json
config_version: 1
name: shop
model_paths: [models]
python_paths: ["."]            # default; model modules are imported relative to these roots
vars:
  country: BR
models:                        # folder config, from 0.9
  +materialized: table         # root +keys are project defaults
  +retries: 1
  +timeout: 30m
  marts:
    +tags: [daily]
sources:                       # source groups, from 0.9
  raw:
    format: parquet
    location: data/raw
    tables:
      orders:
        location: orders/
      customers:
        location: customers/
targets:
  dev:
    engine:
      kind: polars
    catalog:
      kind: filesystem
      root: ./warehouse
    naming:
      kind: per_user
    state:
      kind: sqlite
      path: .pipeloom/state.db
    workers: 4
  prod:
    engine:
      kind: spark
    catalog:
      kind: unity
      catalog: main
    naming:
      kind: prefix
      schema_prefix: prod_
    state:
      kind: table
      table: ops._pipeloom_state
    artifacts:
      root: /Volumes/main/ops/pipeloom
    deploy:                                  # 0.5: a plugin block, validated against `renderers`
      kind: databricks
      pipelines:
        main: {}
        daily:
          select: ["tag:daily"]
      compute:
        default:
          kind: serverless
          environment_version: "5"
      task_grouping: none
events:
  sinks:
    - kind: console
    - kind: jsonl
      path: target/events.jsonl
      failure_budget: 5

Sources (from 0.9). sources maps a group name to format, location, schema, options, tags, meta and tables. A table may set the same keys plus location or table: a table location is joined to the group location, a table table is qualified by the group schema. A table entry whose merged result has no location and no table uses its key as table, qualified by the group schema; one with both is PLS108. targets.<t>.sources.<group> deep-merges over the group, and an explicit null removes a key, so a prod target can read the same tables from a catalog. Sources in properties files are rejected for now.

Models (from 0.9). A model is a function marked with @model in any *.py file under model_paths (a directory scanned recursively, or a glob) or inside a package named in model_packages. Every model file must lie under a python_paths root.

from pipeloom import ModelContext, Write, model

@model(materialized="incremental",
       incremental={"input": "orders", "column": "updated_at", "lookback": "2d"},
       write=Write(strategy="merge", unique_key=["order_id"]))
def fct_orders(ctx: ModelContext, orders, stg_customers):
    return ctx.sql("select o.*, c.name from orders o join stg_customers c using (customer_id)")
  • Parameters are the inputs. Each binds in this order: (1) an inputs= entry (ref(...), source(...) or a bare name, which resolves by steps 3 and 4); (2) a parameter with a default is never an input unless inputs= lists it; (3) a model of that name other than the model itself; (4) a source table of that name when exactly one group has it; (5) anything else is PLR201. A table name in two groups is PLR210. ctx is optional and reserved.
  • The default name is the function name, and a file may hold several models. Decorator arguments use the YAML keys, as plain dicts or as the re-exported config models (Write, Incremental, Column, Expectation, Quality, Deletes, DataTest), plus the helpers ref, source, var and the check helpers (not_null, unique, accepted_values, between, regex, row_count, freshness).
  • SQL runs through ctx.sql(query, *, dialect=None, inputs=None) against the inputs by alias (section 5). There are no SQL model files.

Properties files (from 0.9). Any *.yml or *.yaml under model_paths except pipeloom.yml. They describe and configure models; they never create one or set inputs.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://emanuel-luis.github.io/pipeloom/latest/schema/v1/properties.json
models:
  - name: fct_orders
    description: One row per order.
    config:
      partition_by: [order_date]
      tags: [finance]
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        dtype: int64
        nullable: false
    data_tests:
      - name: order_id_unique
        check:
          unique: [order_id]
        on_violation: fail

An entry that names no model, or a model another entry already describes, is PLR209 (suppressed while any PLY005 exists). unit_tests also live here (ADR-0045).

Discovery (from 0.9). One scan of model_paths and model_packages finds model modules and properties files. - An AST pass parses every .py file that imports pipeloom. A @model on a top-level def whose arguments are all static (literals, containers of static values, or calls to known helpers and re-exported config classes on static values) is resolved without importing the module. Any other use makes the module dynamic. Unknown keywords are PLS101 from the AST in both cases. - Dynamic modules, and only those, are imported through pipeloom.discovery.loader.ModuleLoader, which puts the python_paths roots on sys.path under a process-wide lock and purges the project's modules on exit. Each module that cannot be loaded is one PLY005; loading never stops at the first. - <project>/.pipeloom/cache/discovery.json caches static results per file, keyed by path, mtime_ns, size and the pipeloom and Python versions. Dynamic modules are always imported again. The cache is never part of the manifest or the plan hash, and a failed write is ignored. - Discovery.refresh() re-reads changed files and re-imports dynamic modules for long-lived processes such as docs serve. - An executor running a unit from a manifest never runs discovery: it imports the one module named by its node's callable. Any invocation that compiles runs discovery, including pipeloom run without --manifest and every unit task in Airflow PROJECT mode, so dynamic modules are imported there too.

Model-only keys (0.9, ADR-0045), which the models: tree cannot set: unit_tests (cases {name, given, expect}, given keyed by input alias, the parameter name of a decorated function), set in the model's properties entry; and data_tests ({name, check: {not_null | unique | relationships: {column, to: {ref | source}, field}}, on_violation: warn | fail}), set by the decorator's data_tests= or by properties, where the decorator list replaces the properties list. Unit tests stay out of the manifest; data_tests appears as nodes[].data_tests and enters the node checksum only when declared.

YAML model files (0.8 and earlier). Model entries with sql: or python:, flat sources: lists, _defaults.yml and defaults.models were removed in 0.9 with no deprecation release; their keys are PLS101 with a hint to the migration guide, and PLK601, PLK604, PLC502 and PLR205 are retired.

ADR-0050: Python-first model authoring (supersedes ADR-0003, which made YAML declare every model). - Context: a YAML-declared Python model was written twice, once in YAML and once as a function whose parameters had to match (PLK602). A benchmark of 1,000 models measured about 11 s to import every module and 1.4 s to parse them with ast. - Options: keep YAML-first; Python-first with static discovery only (no computed config); Python-first importing every module (slow, runs user code on every compile); Python-first with hybrid discovery. - Choice: hybrid. Every model is a decorated Python function; YAML holds the project, folder config, sources, targets and properties. The compiler resolves static decorators from the AST and imports only dynamic modules, with a per-file cache. SQL runs through ctx.sql. Dependencies stay declared through parameters and inputs=, never traced. - Consequences: a model is written once, with typed completion. Most compiles run no user code; a dynamic module runs its code at compile time. Every project is rewritten once, with no deprecation release, and plan hashes change once.

JSON Schema. pipeloom schema export --out schemas/ writes project.json and properties.json (draft 2020-12) from the pydantic models. models.json and defaults.json are no longer published under latest/ since 0.9 (older version folders keep them). - Plugin option models (engine, catalog, sink, state) are composed as oneOf branches on kind, using the plugins that are installed (--plugins builtin limits it to the built-ins). - The docs site publishes the schemas of the built-in plugins under latest/schema/v1/ (and under each version folder). - The modeline above enables completion in editors that use yaml-language-server.

Precedence. - Runtime settings (highest first): CLI flags; PIPELOOM_* environment variables (for example PIPELOOM_TARGET, PIPELOOM_WORKERS); an optional git-ignored user file ~/.pipeloom/profiles.yml with per-target overrides; the targets.<t> block; then top-level project keys. - Model config: the @model decorator; then the config of the model's properties entry; then the models: tree from the folder nearest the model up to the root; then the root +keys; then built-in defaults. Mappings deep-merge, lists replace, tags is an ordered union and an explicit null removes a key (YAML only). columns is a model key that the folder tree cannot set, and decorator columns replace properties columns whole. ResolvedModel.origins records the layer and location of each top-level key, so a diagnostic points at the layer that set the value; origins are not in the manifest. - Targets may change runtime keys (engine options, catalog, naming, state, workers, artifacts, deploy) and, from 0.9, override source groups (targets.<t>.sources: format, location, schema, options, tables). deploy is a runtime key like the others: the target block wins over the top-level one. The core validates its options with the config_model of the renderers plugin it names (the factory is never called), records them in the manifest as metadata.deploy (not part of the plan hash) and resolves nothing in them at runtime except ${secret:...} references in plugin options. They may not change model semantics, so plans differ across targets only in physical names, source relations and runtime settings. - Interpolation: ${env:NAME}, ${env:NAME:-default} and ${var:name} resolve at compile time and are recorded in the manifest. ${secret:provider/path} resolves only at runtime (section 14).

docs.title: 5. Core protocols
docs.text:
from typing import Any, Protocol, Mapping, Sequence, Iterator, ContextManager
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Column: name: str; dtype: str; nullable: bool = True   # logical type: int64, decimal(18,2), timestamp[UTC]...
Schema = tuple[Column, ...]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Relation:                      # opaque handle; never inspected by core
    native: Any                      # pandas/polars frame, Spark DataFrame...
    engine: str
    lazy: bool

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EngineCapabilities:
    formats: frozenset[str]; strategies: frozenset[str]
    sql_models: bool; views: bool; idempotent_writes: bool
    cancel: bool; bytes_metrics: bool; portable: bool   # Narwhals-compatible frames
    quality: bool                                       # evaluate and apply_drops (0.3)
    materializations: frozenset[str]                    # table, view, ephemeral (0.2)
    sql_dialect: str | None = None                      # sqlglot dialect for ctx.sql (0.9, ADR-0050)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StateStoreCapabilities: shared: bool              # visible to every process and task of a run

class Engine(Protocol):
    name: str
    version: str                                       # recorded as engine_version in run_results
    capabilities: EngineCapabilities
    def session(self, ctx: "RuntimeContext", *, catalog: "Catalog") -> ContextManager["EngineSession"]: ...  # one per invocation, thread-safe, cleanup guaranteed (L10)

class EngineSession(Protocol):
    native: Any                                        # escape hatch
    def reader(self, fmt: str) -> "Reader": ...
    def materializer(self, strategy: str) -> "Materializer": ...
    def sql(self, query: str, inputs: Mapping[str, Relation]) -> Relation: ...
    def schema(self, rel: Relation) -> Schema: ...
    def count(self, rel: Relation) -> int: ...
    def filter_since(self, rel: Relation, column: str, lower: Any, *, inclusive: bool = True) -> Relation: ...  # strict (>) when not inclusive
    def relation(self, native: Any) -> Relation: ...   # check a model's return value and wrap it; TypeError for a foreign type
    def persist(self, rel: Relation) -> Relation: ...  # in-memory copy for results shared by several units
    def create_view(self, target: "TargetRef", query: str, inputs: Mapping[str, "ReadSpec"]) -> "WriteResult": ...  # catalog view, never a session view
    def max_value(self, rel: Relation, column: str) -> Any: ...      # a plain Python value, never numpy or pandas
    def evaluate(self, rel: Relation, checks: Sequence["ExpectationSpec"]) -> "QualityCounts": ...  # raw counts; the core judges
    def apply_drops(self, rel: Relation, checks: Sequence["ExpectationSpec"], *, quarantine: "QuarantineMeta | None") -> "DropResult": ...
    def align(self, rel: Relation, schema: Schema) -> Relation: ...  # schema order, missing columns as typed nulls, cast
    def write_intermediate(self, rel: Relation, ref: "IntermediateRef", token: str) -> "WriteResult": ...  # overwrite at ref.location; a repeated token writes nothing (0.4)
    def applied_token(self, target: "TargetRef", token: str) -> "WriteResult | None": ...  # stored result with skipped=True
    def unit_scope(self, unit_id: str) -> ContextManager[None]: ...  # tags this thread's work so cancel can find it
    def is_transient(self, exc: BaseException) -> bool | None: ...   # True retryable, False permanent, None no opinion
    def cancel(self, unit_id: str) -> None: ...        # cooperative; no-op if not capable

class Reader(Protocol):
    def read(self, spec: "ReadSpec") -> Relation: ...            # source or upstream target
class Writer(Protocol):                                           # format-level primitive
    def write(self, rel: Relation, target: "TargetRef", mode: str, opts: "WriteOptions") -> None: ...

class Materializer(Protocol):                                     # one per strategy
    strategy: str
    def materialize(self, rel: Relation, target: "TargetRef", cfg: "WriteConfig",
                    token: str) -> "WriteResult": ...             # token = idempotency key; cfg.run_started_at = the run's start (the session opens before it is resolved)

class Catalog(Protocol):
    def exists(self, target: "TargetRef") -> bool: ...
    def ensure_namespace(self, ns: "Namespace") -> None: ...      # idempotent, cached per invocation
    def table_schema(self, target: "TargetRef") -> Schema | None: ...
    def apply_grants(self, target: "TargetRef", grants: Sequence["Grant"]) -> None: ...
    def maintain(self, target: "TargetRef", ops: Sequence["MaintenanceOp"]) -> None: ...  # explicit (L8)

class MetricsProvider(Protocol):                      # plugin-internal since 0.4: not part of the core API
    def before_write(self, target: "TargetRef") -> "MetricsToken": ...
    def after_write(self, target: "TargetRef", token: "MetricsToken", result: "WriteResult") -> "WriteMetrics": ...

class StateStore(Protocol):
    def get_watermark(self, key: "StateKey") -> "Watermark | None": ...
    def cas_watermark(self, key: "StateKey", expected: "Watermark | None", new: "Watermark") -> bool: ...
    def record_run(self, record: "RunRecord") -> None: ...           # insert or replace
    def get_run(self, run_id: str) -> "RunRecord | None": ...
    def record_unit(self, record: "UnitRecord") -> None: ...         # keyed by (run_id, unit_id, attempt)
    def list_units(self, run_id: str) -> tuple["UnitRecord", ...]: ...  # sorted by (unit_id, attempt)
    def list_runs(self, project: str, target: str, limit: int, before: str | None = None) -> tuple["RunRecord", ...]: ...  # 0.9: newest first; before is a run id
    def lock(self, scope: str, run_id: str) -> ContextManager["LockInfo"]: ...  # non-blocking; raises LockHeld; 60 s lease renewed every 20 s
    def close(self) -> None: ...

class EventSink(Protocol):
    name: str
    def handle(self, event: "Event") -> None: ...
    def flush(self) -> None: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

class Renderer(Protocol):
    name: str
    def render(self, plan: "Plan", options: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Mapping[str, bytes]: ...  # path -> content
    # 0.5: the core only binds a renderer's options; it never builds one. The Databricks plugin
    # keeps rendering internal (`render_job`) and exposes `pipeloom_databricks.api`, so this
    # protocol stays a plugin-internal convention and is not called by the core.

class Executor(Protocol):
    name: str
    boundary: str                                    # "process" | "task"
    def submit(self, unit_id: str, *, queued_at: float) -> "UnitHandle": ...
    def wait_any(self, timeout: float | None) -> "UnitCompletion | None": ...  # None on timeout or wake
    def cancel(self, handle: "UnitHandle", reason: str, *, final: bool = False) -> bool: ...  # timeout and final also abandon the unit
    def has_terminal_event(self, handle: "UnitHandle") -> bool: ...  # a child process already emitted its own
    def wake(self) -> None: ...                      # unblocks wait_any; safe from a signal handler
    def shutdown(self, *, wait: bool) -> None: ...

class Clock(Protocol):
    def now(self) -> datetime: ...                   # timezone-aware UTC
    def monotonic(self) -> float: ...

class IdentityProvider(Protocol):
    def current(self) -> "Identity": ...             # user, host, orchestrator, orchestrator ids

class SecretProvider(Protocol):
    def resolve(self, path: str) -> str: ...

The engine protocols above omit Writer, Catalog.apply_grants and Catalog.maintain; they arrive with the versions that need them (section 16). MetricsProvider is shown for the shape of the before_write and after_write pair; with one implementation, the Spark engine's DeltaMetrics, it stays plugin-internal in 0.4 and the core has no such protocol. ReadSpec.format accepts "table" to read a catalog table through ReadSpec.table. The plugin API is (0, 2) in 0.2 (ADR-0021) and (0, 3) in 0.3 (ADR-0024) and (0, 4) in 0.4 (ADR-0030) and (0, 5) in 0.9 (ADR-0047); while the major version is 0 a plugin must match exactly.

0.3 contract additions. - WriteConfig carries strategy, unique_key, partition_by, update_condition (engine dialect; source. and target. qualifiers, a bare name means source), deletes (DeleteSpec), columns (the final schema, chosen by the core) and commit_meta. - WriteResult(rows_inserted, rows_updated, rows_deleted, rows_written, bytes_written, target_version, skipped, commit_meta). commit_meta is stored with the idempotency token and returned on a replay, so a replayed write hands back the watermark and the quality summary of the original attempt. - evaluate and apply_drops need the quality capability. Engines count and split rows; the core judges (section 10). - pipeloom.engine.errors: TransientError (raise it to force a retryable failure), CommitConflict (a transient error for a table commit race) and WriteKeyError (PLM206). - pipeloom.engine.types also holds ColumnChange, SchemaDiff, ExpectationSpec, QualityCounts, QuarantineMeta, DropResult, can_widen and diff_schemas.

0.4 contract additions (plugin API (0, 4), ADR-0030). - RuntimeContext gains run_started_at (timezone-aware UTC, the same in every invocation of a run) and artifacts_root (absolute POSIX path or URI). The engine session opens before any state-store call and before the run lock, so it has no run_started_at; the core passes it in WriteConfig.run_started_at and IntermediateRef.run_started_at. - EngineSession.write_intermediate(rel, ref, token) persists an intermediate model at IntermediateRef.location; ReadSpec(format="intermediate", location=...) reads it back. - CatalogCapabilities(views=) is static data on a catalog spec, so L5 can report PLC507 without importing the catalog. - unit_scope spans a unit's reads, body, checks and write, because a lazy engine does its work at the write. - WriteRefusedError is what an engine raises when its idempotency guard refuses a write; the core reports PLM207 (section 7).

0.9 contract additions (plugin API (0, 5), ADR-0047). - StateStore.list_runs(project, target, limit, before=None) returns the runs of one project and target, newest first by (started_at, run_id), at most limit; before is a run id to page from, and an unknown one raises UnknownRun. pipeloom.state.types.page_runs does the ordering and paging for any store. The core calls it through pipeloom.state.types.list_runs, which raises ListRunsUnsupported (PLX117) for a store that lacks the method. - EngineSession.from_rows(rows, schema) -> Relation, to_rows(rel) -> list[dict] (plain Python values) and orphans(rel, column, parent, field) -> int (child rows whose non-null key has no parent row; NaN is null, parent nulls never match) serve unit tests and relationships data tests (ADR-0045). pipeloom.engine.portable has to_rows and an anti-join orphans for narwhals engines; Spark counts orphans with a left_anti join. An engine without them fails only when a test uses them (PLX115). - EngineCapabilities.sql_dialect (0.9, ADR-0050) names the engine's sqlglot dialect, or None. It is part of (0, 5), which is unreleased, so the version does not change.

ModelContext.sql (0.9, ADR-0050). ModelContext keeps its fields and gains sql(query, *, dialect=None, inputs=None), backed by a private callable the runner sets. The query sees the model's inputs by alias as read (after the incremental filter); inputs= adds or replaces frames by name. It returns the native frame, or a Narwhals frame under frame_api: narwhals. The dialect is the dialect argument, then the inheritable model setting sql_dialect, then the engine's own. Only when the chosen dialect differs from the engine's does pipeloom.runtime.sql translate the query with sqlglot transpile, imported lazily; without the sqlglot extra that is PLC513. pandas has no SQL and raises SqlUnsupportedError (PLX101 with a hint); L6 warns with PLK606 beforehand. In a view model the runner calls the function in view mode and ctx.sql returns a ViewQuery for create_view; any other return value is PLX120. The function is called by keyword: the input aliases, plus ctx when it is a parameter.

ADR-0002: Engine abstraction. - Context: the spec (section 4) lists coupling in the return type, reads, schema, temporary views, writes, merge, metrics and catalog SQL. - Options: - (a) A hand-written protocol per plugin: full control, more code per engine. - (b) Narwhals as the core abstraction: it has no write, SQL or catalog API, and only lazy PySpark. - (c) Ibis: heavy, its write support is unverified, and it pushes users into an expression API. - (d) A hybrid. - Choice: (d). - The core contract is the hand-written protocols above. Plugins own IO, writes, merge, catalogs, metrics and cancellation. - The core depends on Narwhals (it has no dependencies of its own) only for pipeloom.engine.portable. That module gives default count, filter_since, max_value, schema and evaluate that pandas, polars and PySpark plugins may reuse, through narwhals.stable.v2. - Model bodies receive native frames by default. frame_api: narwhals on a model passes Narwhals frames, so portable models work on any engine with capabilities.portable. - Consequences: no lowest-common-denominator API for Spark users. Engines can override portable defaults for speed. Narwhals stays a replaceable implementation detail.

docs.title: 6. Plugin system and plugin API version
docs.text:
ADR-0004: Discovery. - Options: entry points (stdlib importlib.metadata, the pytest model), pluggy (1:N hook fan-out), or a dbt-style namespace import. - Choice: entry points. pipeloom picks one implementation per role by kind, which is 1-of-N selection, not hook fan-out, so pluggy adds a dependency without a matching need.

Groups: - pipeloom.engines - pipeloom.catalogs - pipeloom.state_stores - pipeloom.sinks - pipeloom.secret_providers - pipeloom.executors - pipeloom.renderers - pipeloom.naming - pipeloom.commands (0.5, ADR-0034): a Click command or group that a plugin adds to the pipeloom CLI. pipeloom plugins list --group commands lists them from metadata; a command is imported only when invoked, built-in names win and a command that cannot be imported exits 1.

Each entry point resolves to a PluginSpec(name, kind, api_version: tuple[int, int], factory, config_model, compatible_engines).

Rules: - Discovery reads metadata only. A plugin is imported only when a config names its kind. - pipeloom plugins list imports nothing. - PIPELOOM_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 restricts loading to --plugin module:spec. - Duplicate kind names within a group are error PLU002.

Plugin API version. pipeloom.plugins.API_VERSION = (MAJOR, MINOR), independent of the package version. - MINOR covers additive changes: new optional protocol methods with defaults, new capabilities. - MAJOR covers breaking protocol changes. - In 1.x nothing is added to EngineSession or StateStore. An optional member gets its own small typing.Protocol and a core helper with a fallback, like pipeloom.state.types.list_runs (ADR-0016, amendment 1.1). - The core accepts plugins with the same MAJOR and MINOR ≤ its own. Otherwise it raises PLU001 naming the installed and required versions. - The plugin API is (1, 0). Before 1.0 it was 0.x with an exact match, so a plugin built for (0, 5) fails with PLU001. - config_version: 1 is the only accepted value through 1.x (CONFIG_VERSION in pipeloom.config.types). - Every distribution declares config-version and plugin-api in a [tool.pipeloom] table. tools/versions.py check compares them with CONFIG_VERSION and API_VERSION in the source and requires every PluginSpec to pass API_VERSION.

docs.text:
Each finding is a Diagnostic(code, severity, message, hint, location{file,line,col,json_pointer}, context). Diagnostics serialize to JSON. The catalog lives in code (pipeloom.diagnostics.codes) and generates the docs page. Codes are never reused.
