Polars 2.0 DataFrame engine CI against 2.0 now (1.0.x patch). Narwhals Frame API over many backends The portable layer. Cross-engine matrix (1.1). delta-rs Delta without Spark Delta targets and state store (1.8). PyIceberg 0.12.0 Iceberg catalogs and tables Stretch in 1.8. Write support is unverified. Behavior only, no source reading (Databricks License, not OSI). Soda Core Data quality checks Behavior only (Elastic License 2.0). Great Expectations (GX Core) Expectations Context only. Fivetran is its steward. datacontract-cli and ODCS Contract import, export, breaking checks ODCS export (1.5). pandera DataFrame schema checks Left to the community (bridge plugin rejected). OpenLineage Lineage events and facets Facet pass (1.6). OpenTelemetry CI/CD conventions Tracing, release-candidate conventions pipeloom-otel (1.6). sqlglot SQL parsing and column lineage Column lineage (1.6). Pinned to a tested range.

docs.text: Tool What it does Relevance to pipeloom dlt Python EL library EL-then-T recipe (1.3 stretch). Lakeflow Connect Managed lakehouse ingestion Freshness checks cover it. Sling EL tool Subprocess use only, if ever. dbt-mcp, dagster-io/skills MCP server and agent skills pipeloom-mcp and generated skills (1.2, 1.7). Pathway Streaming Out of scope. Behavior only (BSL).

docs.title: What pipeloom has and lacks
docs.text:
Ahead:

  • Function-first authoring with sqlglot translation.
  • Versioned artifacts with published JSON Schemas and a typed event stream (pipeloom.event/1).
  • Orchestrator renderers built on a unit protocol with a plan-hash guard.
  • Engine-agnostic protocols with conformance suites.
  • An Apache license with no hosted tier, neutral between the Fivetran and dbt group and the Prefect and Dagster group.

Behind:

  • No local SQL engine, no interval or partition backfill model, no plan diff or data diff, no column lineage.
  • No history-based anomaly checks, no agent surface, no dbt migration path.
  • No Iceberg, no Delta writes without Spark, and no first-run demo.

Several gaps that reports listed are already covered in 1.0: warn, drop and fail severity on expectations and data tests, CSV fixtures in unit tests, --full-refresh on run and retry, and the capability checks at validation (only a docs matrix is new). The node checksum does cover config, body, columns and data tests together, which supports the split in 1.2.

docs.title: Where each finding lands
docs.text:
This table maps findings to roadmap releases.

Release Items 1.0.x Polars 2.0 CI, Databricks CLI and Airflow upstream checks 1.1 DuckDB, conformance kit, Narwhals guide and matrix, demo. Stretch: Sail CI recipe, show --limit 1.2 Split checksums, plan diff, table diff, dataset identity, agent surface. Stretch: Slim CI recipe, validate --dry-run 1.3 Intervals, ledger and backfill, outcome fields, cursor options. Stretch: sequence_by, EL-then-T recipe, retry resume set 1.4 Partitions, Airflow and Databricks work, pipeloom-dagster. Stretch: orchestrator conformance kit, Prefect recipe 1.5 Freshness and anomaly checks, reconcile, skip-unchanged, schema contracts, ODCS export. Stretch: ODCS import, unit-test upgrades, prune 1.6 Column lineage, OpenLineage facets, OpenTelemetry. Stretch: UC external lineage push, query annotations 1.7 Read layer, grouping, MCP server, UI. Stretch: profile 1.8 Delta without a cluster, Iceberg on Spark 1.9 Language server and VS Code extension. Stretch: model parameterization, access and deprecation_date Rejected or deferred See the rejected list in the roadmap Not placed Delta change data feed

docs.title: Pitfalls taken from the code readings
docs.text:
• Hash false positives: dbt regressed repeatedly on whitespace normalization. Hash normalized ASTs, version the algorithm and ship an explainer.
  • Deferral computed twice produces disagreeing layers. Compute the map once, in the plan.
  • Microbatch traps: silent full scans without event_time, ephemeral upstreams, lookback off-by-one, and timezone and DST handling.
  • Lineage overconfidence: sqlglot lineage misses indirect dependencies, so record completeness per column.
  • Dataset identity drift between assets and lineage: define one canonical function early.
  • Observers must never change results: a lineage failure never changes the exit code.
  • WATCHER at scale: hanging sensors, stacked retry delays, Variable writes and XCom growth.
  • Select and exclude on a narrowed set: evaluate both on the full graph.
  • Semantic-layer scope creep: export only.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walks through a small project with one source and two models, then runs it on polars.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
$ pip install "pipeloom[polars]"

Use pipeloom[pandas] for the pandas engine and pipeloom[duckdb] for DuckDB. Add the sqlglot extra to get warnings about SQL that reads tables you did not declare (pipeloom[polars,sqlglot]).

docs.title: Try it in one command
docs.text:
With the DuckDB engine installed, one command writes a sample project, builds it and writes the docs site, with nothing else to set up:

$ uvx --from "pipeloom[duckdb]" pipeloom demo

It prints the path of target/docs/index.html in the new pipeloom_demo folder and the commands to try next. See pipeloom demo.

Two ways in: the demo, or init, validate and run. Source: quickstart.d2.

docs.title: Start from pipeloom init
docs.text:
The fastest start is to let pipeloom write the project:

$ pipeloom init shop
Project name [shop]:
Engine (polars, pandas, spark, databricks, duckdb) [polars]:
Created project 'shop' (polars) in shop
Next steps:
  cd shop
  pipeloom validate
  pipeloom run

It writes pipeloom.yml with a dev target, a source group and a models: tree, one decorated model in each of models/bronze, models/silver and models/gold, a properties file models/silver/_properties.yml, a small CSV in data/, a .gitignore and a README. Pass --no-input (and --name, --engine, --catalog) to skip the questions; see pipeloom init.

Every YAML file starts with a schema modeline, and .vscode/settings.json maps the published schemas to the project files. With only the YAML extension (redhat.vscode-yaml, recommended in .vscode/extensions.json), VS Code completes keys and flags mistakes as you type.

docs.title: Add a model
docs.text:
$ pipeloom new model customers_clean --folder silver
models/silver/customers_clean.py
$ pipeloom validate

pipeloom new model NAME writes one .py file under models/ with a function decorated with @model. By default its body returns ctx.sql("select 1 as id"), or, when the default target is pandas, a frame stub; pass --sql or --python to choose. Add a parameter for each input, named like the model or source table it reads, then fill in the body. See pipeloom new.

The rest of this page writes a project by hand, to show each part.

docs.title: Write the project
docs.text:
pipeloom.yml:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://emanuel-luis.github.io/pipeloom/latest/schema/v1/project.json
config_version: 1
name: shop
sources:
  raw:
    format: csv
    location: raw
    tables:
      orders:
        location: orders.csv
targets:
  dev:
    engine:
      kind: polars
    catalog:
      kind: filesystem
      root: target/warehouse
    state:
      kind: json
      path: .pipeloom/state

raw/orders.csv:

id,customer_id,amount
1,10,5.0
2,10,2.5
3,11,7.0

models/orders.py:

from pipeloom import ModelContext, model


@model(tags=["staging"])
def stg_orders(ctx: ModelContext, orders):
    return ctx.sql("select id, customer_id, amount from orders")


@model
def orders_by_customer(ctx: ModelContext, stg_orders):
    return ctx.sql(
        "select customer_id, sum(amount) as total from stg_orders group by customer_id"
    )

A model is a function marked with @model. Its parameters are its inputs: orders binds to the source table raw.orders, and stg_orders to the model of that name. ctx.sql runs a query over the inputs by parameter name and returns the engine's frame; a model may also build and return a frame itself. Settings such as tags are @model keywords, or folder defaults in a models: tree in pipeloom.yml. Coming from 0.8 and YAML models? See Migrating from 0.8.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
$ pipeloom validate
Project 'shop' is valid.

validate runs every layer from YAML syntax to the capability check of your engine. Findings print to stderr with a code such as PLR201; the error codes page explains each one.

docs.title: Explore the graph
docs.text:
$ pipeloom ls --select tag:staging
stg_orders
$ pipeloom graph
stg_orders
orders_by_customer <- stg_orders

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
$ pipeloom run
... 1/2 OK     stg_orders ............. table/overwrite        3 rows ...
... 2/2 OK     orders_by_customer ..... table/overwrite        2 rows ...

Each model is now a table under target/warehouse/main/. Rerun with the same --run-id and the data stays byte-identical. See Running a pipeline.

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
$ ls target
manifest.json  run_results.json  runs  warehouse

run_results.json has one row per model with its status, timing, rows and bytes written and schema hash; the manifest lists every model, source and execution unit, with a plan_hash that changes when the pipeline changes. See Run artifacts.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Status: plan as of 2026-11-21, written against 1.1.0. Versions 0.8 to 1.1 are delivered; this page now plans 1.2 to 1.9 and lists the breaking changes the stability policy holds back. Section 16 of architecture.md keeps the record of what each delivered version contains. The market research behind the plan is in Market landscape. Items that change a decision name the ADR they need: ADRs up to 0050 exist and are accepted, and new ones continue from 0051.

Terms such as unit, run, boundary and artifacts root are defined in the glossary. In short, a unit is one schedulable node of the plan (a persisted model plus the ephemeral models inlined into it), and the artifacts root is the folder where each run writes its manifest, results, events and logs.

The maintainer settled the open choices of this plan on 2026-11-20. Section 6 records each one and the alternative it replaced. Scope inside a version can still move while its ADR is written.

docs.title: 1. Vision and principles
docs.text:
pipeloom should make a pipeline cheap to write, check and run anywhere: one project of Python models, one compiled plan, any engine, any orchestrator, and every run observable without extra code. The roadmap borrows the developer experience of dbt, the orchestrator integration of astronomer-cosmos and the plan and diff safety of SQLMesh. It leaves out the parts that would make pipeloom heavier: Jinja, a server process and a portable SQL dialect.

The 13 principles in section 1 of the architecture still apply. These five guide the choices below:

  1. Simplicity first. A feature that only needs a flag gets a flag, not a new subsystem. New commands reuse pipeloom.api.Project and the existing stages.
  2. Engine-agnostic. Every new feature goes through the existing protocols (EngineSession, Catalog, StateStore, EventSink) or declares the capability it needs.
  3. Artifacts are the integration contract. Exporters, the docs site, the UI and lineage read manifest.json, run_results.json, the event JSONL and the attempt files, and never reach into the runtime.
  4. Observable by default. Every new behavior emits typed events on the bus (pipeloom.events), and every consumer is a sink.
  5. Export over lock-in. pipeloom renders to orchestrators and leaves scheduling, job-level retries and any UI that triggers runs to them.

The non-goals are listed in section 5. Several change in this plan, and each change says what it was before.

docs.title: The UI non-goal
docs.text: Since ADR-0043 the non-goal is "a scheduler service, or any UI that starts, schedules or changes runs". A read-only viewer over the artifacts root and the state store is allowed. It reads local or mounted paths, listens on localhost by default and ships as a separate distribution, so the core stays small.

docs.title: 2. Where pipeloom stands at 1.0
docs.text:
• Authoring: Python models marked with @model, YAML for the project and properties files, SQL through ctx.sql, five materializations, write strategies (append, overwrite, replace_partitions, merge with deletes, scd2), per-model catalogs, contracts, unit and data tests, and ${env}, ${var} and ${secret} interpolation.
  • Validation: layers L0 to L6 with file, line and column diagnostics, a generated error catalog and published JSON Schemas under schema/v1/.
  • CLI: init, new model, validate, compile, ls, run, build, test, retry, finalize, graph, docs, explain, runs, schema, plugins, plus plugin commands.
  • Runtime: a ready-queue scheduler, thread and process executors, retries, timeouts, cancellation, idempotent writes, watermarks, expectations with quarantine, state:modified selection and --defer.
  • Observability: the pipeloom.event/1 stream, console, jsonl, webhook and OpenLineage sinks, run history through list_runs, and versioned artifact schemas.
  • Export and engines: polars, pandas and Spark with Delta; Databricks jobs and bundles; Airflow in LOCAL, VIRTUALENV, KUBERNETES, DATABRICKS and WATCHER modes. The plugin API is (1, 0).

docs.title: Gaps against the market
docs.text:
Evidence for each row is in Market landscape. The pipeloom 1.0 column comes from a code check on 1.0.

Area pipeloom 1.0 Gap Target Local SQL engine polars, pandas, Spark no DuckDB, which is the usual on-ramp for demos and CI 1.1 First run init no demo with sample data and a docs site in one command 1.1 Change safety one checksum per node, covering config, body, columns and tests no split checksums, no plan diff, no table diff 1.2 Backfills watermark plus lookback no interval windows, no interval ledger, no backfill command 1.3 Partitions in orchestrators assets per unit no partition keys in artifacts, no partitioned Airflow assets 1.4 History-based checks list_runs, expectations with warn, drop or fail no freshness, no volume change, no anomaly score, no reconciliation 1.5 Column lineage none nodes[].column_lineage not computed 1.6 Agent and UI surface docs site no generated agent skills, no read layer, no MCP server, no pipeloom ui 1.2, 1.7 Open table formats Delta through Spark no Delta without a cluster, no Iceberg 1.8 Editor support JSON Schema and modeline no language server 1.9

docs.title: 3. Themes
docs.text:
• Engines and the first hour (1.1, 1.8). DuckDB, a conformance kit that third parties can run, and a one-command demo. Delta without a cluster and Iceberg come later.
  • Change intelligence (1.2, 1.6). Split checksums, then plan diff and table diff, then column lineage. This delivers the main value of SQLMesh plans without virtual environments.
  • Intervals and orchestrators (1.3, 1.4). A ledger of processed windows, a backfill command, then partitions reaching Airflow and Databricks.
  • Trust from run history (1.5). Freshness, volume, anomaly and reconciliation checks, schema contracts, and opt-in skipping of unchanged units.
  • Agents and people (1.2, 1.7, 1.9). Machine-readable output and generated skills, a shared read layer, MCP, the UI and the language server.

Rules that hold for every 1.x release:

  • The plugin API gets at most one minor bump per release.
  • An optional protocol member lives in its own small Protocol and is reached through a core helper with a fallback, the way state.types.list_runs works today. Nothing is added to EngineSession or StateStore in 1.x.
  • Anything that tracks a moving upstream ships as experimental.
  • The 1.0 goldens must validate against the current /1 schemas, and the current output must validate against the 1.0 schemas. CI guards both from 1.1.
  • Every release that changes user config ships a migrate-1.x guide page, and every new command or flag gets a guide page and a CLI reference entry. Each release adds an Upgrading section to the changelog.
  • Every ADR from 0051 on carries a Provenance line: the design comes from public docs and observed behavior, and no code was copied.
  • Output that can carry row data (diff markdown, CI summaries, MCP, ui export) shows counts and schema only by default. Samples need an explicit opt-in flag, and columns tagged sensitive in contracts are masked.

Stability lifecycle, to be written into stability.md with the 1.1 ADR: an experimental feature is promoted or removed within two minors, only the latest minor gets patches, and security fixes go to the latest minor.

docs.title: 4. Milestones
docs.text:
Each milestone has one headline and is sized for one maintainer. Releases are time-boxed with a cut date, and stretch items are cut first.

Summary by version:

Version Headline What you can do after it Status 0.8 to 1.0 First hour, Python-first authoring, stable contracts Author, validate, run and export projects with published schemas Delivered 1.0.x Upstream patches Run on Polars 2.0, the current Databricks CLI and Airflow 3.3 and 3.4 Delivered in 1.1.0 1.1 DuckDB and a one-command demo Run a project and a demo on a laptop with DuckDB Delivered 1.2 Know what a change does before it merges See the effect of a change with plan diff and table diff before merging Planned 1.3 Intervals and backfills Backfill a date range and rerun only the missing windows Planned 1.4 Orchestrators run partitions Run one partition from Airflow, Databricks or Dagster Planned 1.5 Run history does the work Catch stale or unusual data from run history Planned 1.6 Lineage and telemetry from the manifest Read column lineage and follow a run as a trace Planned 1.7 One read layer for people and agents Browse runs in a local viewer and query them from an agent (the UI ships as 1.7.x) Planned 1.8 Open table formats without a cluster Write Delta without Spark and Iceberg on Spark Planned 1.9 The editor knows your project Get diagnostics and completion in the editor Planned

docs.title: Delivered
docs.text:
Version What it delivered 0.8 First hour and fast loops: init, new model, explain, state:modified and --defer, retry --from, docs generate and serve (ADR-0042, ADR-0043) 0.9 Python-first authoring (ADR-0050), contracts, unit and data tests, build, SCD2, OpenLineage, run history and webhook, Airflow WATCHER mode (migration guide) 1.0 Stable contracts: published schemas including the manifest, the orchestrator protocol, graph --units, plugin API (1, 0) and the stability policy (ADR-0049) 1.0.x Delivered in 1.1.0, with no 1.0.1 release because nothing was broken for users: Databricks CLI version documentation, the Airflow 3.4 matrix and Polars 2 guards 1.1 Delivered in 1.1.0: DuckDB engine (ADR-0051), conformance kit (ADR-0067), portable models guide and cross-engine matrix, pipeloom demo, init --engine duckdb, experimental tier in the stability policy. The stretch items Sail CI recipe and show --limit did not ship and are dropped

The full list per version is in the CHANGELOG and in section 16 of the architecture.

docs.title: 1.2: Know what a change does before it merges
docs.text:
• Optional checksums{code,config,contract,tests,upstream} and checksum_version on manifest nodes. The 1.0 checksum is unchanged. Sub-selectors state:modified.{code,config,contract,tests,upstream} and ls --why. Config is hashed after ${var} resolution and before ${env} and ${secret}, so secrets are never hashed. ADR: 0052. Done when: A whitespace, comment or docstring edit selects nothing under state:modified.code, while legacy state:modified still selects it. Editing a data test selects only .tests. A 1.0 reference manifest falls back to the legacy checksum with a warning.
  • plan --diff --state <dir> with categories new, removed, breaking, non-breaking, metadata and indirect. A comparison of the old and new SQL syntax trees where an unknown result never counts as safe. Contract gate, --fail-on breaking, plan_diff/1. ADR: 0052. Done when: Fixture pairs give the expected category per unit. A dropped contract column exits 1, and its descendants are indirect-breaking.
  • pipeloom diff <model>: same-engine keyed diff with schema diff, counts and samples, table_diff/1 and markdown. Runs through session.sql or portable frames. The default markdown carries counts and the schema diff only; --samples adds rows, and columns tagged sensitive in contracts are masked. ADR: 0053. Done when: Seeded fixtures on DuckDB and polars give exact matched, partial, source-only and target-only counts. A duplicate key is reported, not a crash. The default markdown contains no cell values.
  • Canonical dataset identity: one pure function in core, with input_assets and output_assets resolved through ephemerals. A hash suffix applies only to names 1.0 rejected. ADR: 0055. Done when: Airflow asset URIs and OpenLineage names for shop and TPC-H are byte-identical to 1.0.0. An ephemeral input resolves to its persisted upstream.
  • Machine-readable diagnostics: --log-format json on the commands that lack it (validate, test), an explain URL on the diagnostic event, and --output json for command results of plan, compile and diff. init writes AGENTS.md and skills generated from the code catalog, init --update-agents regenerates them, and nothing is fetched remotely. Done when: One schema-validated golden per command. A test fails when a catalog code is missing from the skills.
  • Performance budget: a synthetic 1,000-model project with a compile and plan time budget in CI. Done when: CI fails when the budget is exceeded.

Plugin API: unchanged.

Stretch: Slim CI recipe on DuckDB with a step summary and Azure DevOps, validate --dry-run, llms.txt from docs generate, a "Coming from dbt" concept-mapping guide.

docs.title: 1.3: Intervals and backfills
docs.text:
• incremental.interval with event_time, grain, begin and lookback. Half-open UTC windows follow the rounding rules in the dbt microbatch docs. Batches run first, middle, last inside one unit, so the DAG and the renderers stay unchanged. Each interval gets its own idempotency token (for example run_id:model:interval_id) and its own Delta transaction version, as an amendment to ADR-0032. The range replace is an explicit WriteConfig field (replace_range: column, start, end) under the capability interval_writes, so an empty window or a partition coarser than the grain cannot leave stale rows or delete rows outside the window. A missing event_time fails at validation and never becomes a full scan. ADR: 0054 (amends 0032). Done when: Property tests cover the boundary +1 case, month and year truncation, and DST, and run on windows-latest (with a tzdata dependency). A 90-day backfill on Spark/Delta and polars writes exactly 90 windows. An empty window and a month partition under a day grain both leave other rows untouched.
  • Interval ledger: merged intervals stored in the state store under a reserved key (document type pipeloom.intervals/1). The value is a list of ISO-string pairs, because the state codec does not convert datetimes nested in a list. Dev targets never write the prod ledger. The Delta store encodes values through the same codec, so the round trip holds there by code reading. ADR: 0054. Done when: The state contract suite round-trips the ledger on sqlite, json and Delta, and concurrent writers lose no interval.
  • pipeloom backfill --select --start --end [--rerun missing\|all] [--on-failure stop\|continue], deterministic interval ids, restate for a range, and --mark-done to seed the ledger for a model converted from a 1.0 watermark. The migrate-1.x guide covers the conversion. ADR: 0054. Done when: A range with one gap reruns only the gap. --rerun missing after success writes nothing. A killed run resumes only the missing intervals. Converting a 1.0 watermark model reruns zero windows.
  • Outcome fields: documented open skip_reason values (not_selected, up_to_date, not_due, upstream_incomplete) with their failing class listed next to the existing ones, failed_upstream, blocking, and test summaries capped at N ids. No new status. The row schema first splits into the frozen 1.0 required set and optional additions, because every row property is required today, and the test of row defaults changes in the same release. ADR: 0056. Done when: A failing blocking test gives its descendants upstream_failed and failed_upstream. The 1.0 goldens still validate.
  • on_cursor_value_missing: raise\|include\|exclude. Done when: One case file per mode.

Plugin API: (1, 1): optional filter_between in its own Protocol with a portable default, capability interval_writes=False. Validation rejects interval models on engines without it. Fallback: optional StateStore methods in the same bump.

Stretch: sequence_by and ignore-null updates (capability merge_sequencing in the same (1, 1) bump; ties are an error), an EL-then-T recipe with dlt (its end_value overlaps intervals), and, on SIGTERM, signaling the whole process group and printing the retry command and the resume set (Job Objects or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows).

docs.title: 1.4: Orchestrators run partitions
docs.text:
• Typed partition spec derived from the interval. partition_keys in run_results, events and the OpenLineage run facet. Anchored-regex formats checked at validation. A completeness gate returns (satisfied, unreachable, reason). ADR: 0056. Done when: A bad format fails at validate. A missing upstream interval settles with upstream_incomplete. An up_to_date skip still emits the orchestrator signal (or a documented no-op) and counts as non-failing.
  • Airflow work: opt-in experimental partitioned assets, templated emit_assets, WATCHER with bounded XCom and upstream-failed consumers that settle on attempt 1, select and exclude evaluated on the full graph, task ids derived only from unit ids, a 3.2 to 3.4 matrix, and the stable parse-time budget tests. pipeloom-airflow already requires apache-airflow>=3.2,<4, so partitions need no floor change. Done when: The matrix is green. On the Astro example, an asset event with key 2026-11-01 runs exactly that window. A 200-unit WATCHER run with one failure leaves bounded XCom.
  • Databricks work: window_start and window_end job parameters, direct-engine YAML check, CLI range check with a code, the planned load_resources hook. Done when: bundle validate passes on the minimum and latest CLI in CI. A 7-day window run fills the ledger (workspace demo, not in CI).
  • pipeloom-dagster (decided 2026-11-20, see section 6): a new distribution that reads manifest.json and builds one multi_asset per unit, with asset keys from the canonical dataset identity of 1.2. Each materialization runs the unit command of the orchestrator protocol, data tests become asset checks, and interval models map to Dagster time partitions through the partition spec above. Pinned to the public dagster API with a version matrix. ADR: 0066. Done when: the TPC-H polars example loads in dagster dev with one asset per model, materializing one asset runs exactly that unit, a failing data test shows as a failed asset check, and one partition of an interval model runs exactly that window.

Plugin API: unchanged.

Stretch: DOCKER mode and the airflow secret provider (moved out of core to make room for pipeloom-dagster), an orchestrator conformance kit, and a Prefect recipe over graph --units --output json. The airflow dependency group still does not install on Windows (openlineage-sql has no Windows wheel); that stays a documented limit and Airflow development happens on Linux, WSL or CI.

docs.title: 1.5: Run history does the work
docs.text:
• sources freshness, row_count.change_vs_last, and a z-score over comparable runs (window 14, sigma 3, warmup 7). Backfill, full-refresh and retry runs stay out of the baseline, and it resets on a config hash change. Statistics in Python from list_runs. ADR: 0057. Done when: With a FakeClock history, only the injected outlier warns. Fewer than 2 points gives no score.
  • reconcile data test: group_by, filters on both sides, abs or rel tolerance, and groups missing on either side. ADR: 0057. Done when: One missing group and one drifted group are reported on DuckDB and polars.
  • build --skip-unchanged, opt-in. The fingerprint covers the code checksum, config, upstream fingerprints and data versions. The scheduler change is part of the ADR: an up_to_date skip releases children like a success, and the decision happens before QUEUED with a defined state transition. Data versions come from an optional Catalog.data_version(target) in its own Protocol (in-tree engines implement it; when it is missing the unit always runs, with a reason). External writes are not detected unless the engine reports a version. ADR: 0058. Done when: A second identical build runs zero units. Bumping one upstream Delta version reruns only it and its descendants.
  • schema_contract entities (new_table, new_column, type_change) times modes (evolve, fail, drop_value, quarantine_row), with --schema-contract freeze for CI. on_schema_change maps onto it and is deprecated with a warning code, and it keeps working through 1.x. ADR: 0059. Done when: One case per entity and mode on the shared suite. Schema changes in run_results record the entity and the mode.
  • ODCS v3 contract export, sharing one Threshold(op, value) type with the anomaly checks. Lossy mappings are a warning code. Done when: An exported contract validates against the ODCS schema, and a lossy field warns.

Plugin API: (1, 1) if the 1.3 bump is not reused.

Stretch: ODCS import, unit-test upgrades (partial rows, subset mode, tolerance, mocks), pipeloom prune (dry run by default, with a retention floor of at least the largest anomaly window), Unity Catalog metadata push as a diff (an optional Catalog.apply_metadata takes the next API bump).

docs.title: 1.6: Lineage and telemetry from the manifest
docs.text:
• nodes[].column_lineage outside the plan hash, with completeness per column, an indirect pass (filter, join, group, window), a cache keyed by SQL, dialect and schema hash, and lineage --column. sqlglot stays in a tested range bounded by major version, with a weekly job against the latest release and golden lineage tests. ADR: 0060. Done when: TPC-H goldens. The plan hash equals 1.5's. Unqualifiable SQL is marked incomplete and compile exits 0. The performance budget from 1.2 is rechecked.
  • OpenLineage facet pass: columnLineage, dataQualityAssertions, SQL, job type, parent and root run, naming from the 1.2 identity function, and lineage export --run. Done when: Facets validate against the pinned facet schemas. A throwing sink never changes the exit code. Check the spec docs first for whether the 1.53 explicit lineage facets supersede the column facet.
  • pipeloom-otel: the run is the root span, attempts are child spans, and the trace id is derived from run_id. ADR: 0061 (pipeloom.* plus the CI/CD semantic conventions). Done when: A 3-unit process-executor run gives one trace with 3 child spans in an in-memory exporter.

Plugin API: unchanged.

Stretch: UC external lineage push with dry run (verify GA first), Query annotations plus a cost recipe that joins system tables through orchestrator_ids (the optional hook takes the next API bump).

docs.title: 1.7: One read layer for people and agents
docs.text:
The read layer and MCP ship first. The UI follows as 1.7.x with its own cut date, so the largest item cannot hold the release.

  • A read layer over manifest, run_results, events by offset, runs and catalog, placed in pipeloom.artifacts (below docs in the layer contract) and re-exported from pipeloom.api. Docs, UI and MCP all use it. Done when: docs generate output is byte-identical before and after the refactor, and lint-imports passes.
  • group_by in unit_graph (additive /1). File and line already exist on plan nodes. Done when: Goldens updated, and the old goldens still validate.
  • pipeloom-mcp: read-only tools (models, runs, node, explain, plan diff, lineage). No tool runs SQL. Artifact text is wrapped as data, the threat is described in SECURITY.md, and the distribution is separate with an import-linter rule that keeps it out of core. No row data unless the user opts in. ADR: 0062. Done when: An MCP client test lists the tools and asserts none mutates.
  • pipeloom-ui (1.7.x, moved from 1.1): GET only, 127.0.0.1, run picker, DAG colored by the last run, event tail, ui export, path-traversal guard, never imports user code. Host and Origin allowlist, a random session token in the URL, no CORS. ADR: 0062 (server choice). Done when: A test asserts no non-GET route. A foreign Host is rejected. The traversal fuzz test returns 404, with a Windows corpus (drive letters, backslashes, UNC paths, reserved names, case-insensitive matching). Diffs, partitions, anomalies and lineage for TPC-H are viewable.

Plugin API: unchanged.

Stretch: profile and test scaffold.

docs.title: 1.8: Open table formats without a cluster
docs.text:
• Delta targets and a Delta state store through delta-rs for polars, pandas and DuckDB. ADR: 0063. Done when: The Delta contract cells pass on polars and DuckDB. A table written by polars reads in Spark with the same schema.
  • iceberg format in pipeloom-spark against UC or REST catalogs, all strategies. ADR: 0064. Done when: Engine contract cells pass on local Spark with a containerized REST catalog.

Plugin API: unchanged.

Stretch: pyiceberg append and overwrite (current release 0.12.0; verify write support in its docs before writing acceptance criteria), DuckDB attach of DuckLake or Iceberg (DuckLake 1.0 was released on 2026-04-13).

docs.title: 1.9: The editor knows your project
docs.text:
• pipeloom-lsp: diagnostics on save, go-to-definition from a parameter to its model, hover, completion. Works with Windows drive-letter file URIs. ADR: 0065. Done when: A pygls test client drives all four on fixtures/shop.
  • VS Code extension that wraps the LSP and registers the JSON Schemas. A separate repository, or deferred in favor of the schema settings init already writes, because it brings an npm toolchain and publisher tokens outside the current release path. Done when: The extension test opens a project and gets diagnostics.

Plugin API: unchanged.

Stretch: @model.parameterize with literal arguments only, access, groups and deprecation_date.

Parallel work on disjoint files is possible in 1.1 (DuckDB with the kit and the matrix), 1.2 (table diff with the checksums and plan diff), 1.4 (the Airflow work with the Databricks work), 1.6 (OpenTelemetry with column lineage and the facet pass) and 1.8 (delta-rs with Iceberg on Spark).

docs.title: Breaking changes held back
docs.text:
The stability policy keeps these out of every 1.x release. They are listed so that 1.x designs leave room for them. None of them needs a new major today, and no major is planned.

  • New run statuses (cached, partial, warn). Adding a value to a closed enum is breaking, so through 1.x the open skip_reason values carry the same information.
  • Removing deprecated items: on_schema_change (deprecated in 1.5) and the single legacy checksum. Both keep working for the whole major.
  • state:modified switching to the split checksums from 1.2.
  • Making optional plugin members required (filter_between, from_rows, to_rows, apply_metadata), which would remove their fallback helpers.
  • The init default engine moving from polars to DuckDB.
  • Intervals as a value of the closed strategy enum.

Research with no version attached: cross-project refs, the Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines export (it needs its own ADR first), a dbt importer and a community Snowflake engine.

docs.title: 5. Non-goals and risks
docs.text:
Non-goals, with what changes (accepted on 2026-11-20, see section 6). Section 1 of the architecture picks up the new list through the stability ADR amendment in 1.1:

  • Streaming: kept. One sentence is added: reading Auto Loader or Lakeflow Connect landing tables through incremental is supported, and checkpoint-based state is not. Bounded streaming reads (Spark's AvailableNow trigger) are revisited only after Delta change data feed, through its own ADR.
  • Snowflake: was "a Snowflake target before a Snowflake engine exists". New wording: engines beyond polars, pandas, Spark and DuckDB are community plugins tested by the conformance kit.
  • UI: was "a scheduler service, or any UI that starts, schedules or changes runs". New wording: "any UI or agent tool that starts, schedules or changes runs". MCP write tools fall under it.
  • Zero-copy environments: kept. Clone-only dev copies are allowed and promotion is not.
  • User code at compile time: kept. Model factories stay static with literal arguments.
  • New: a semantic layer, cross-engine data diff, and ML anomaly models beyond fixed statistics.
  • Kept as they are: Airflow 2, Jinja, a portable SQL dialect and a scheduler service.

Rejected or deferred, with the reason:

  • Cost fields in run_results: contradicts the decision to keep cost in system tables. 1.6 gets a recipe instead.
  • Snowflake engine: very large effort and no test account.
  • dbt import: L effort and Jinja semantics through the back door. Left as research with no version.
  • Bounded streaming reads (Spark's AvailableNow trigger): a second source of state, and per-batch writes under Spark Connect are unverified.
  • Clone environments: --defer covers most of the value. Revisit on demand.
  • YAML Dag export: the upstream format is experimental.
  • Lakeflow Connect: source freshness covers it.
  • Fabric: no demand.
  • Packages, cross-project refs, semantic export and importers: large effort or scope creep, and importers conflict with "YAML only configures".
  • A unit hook, state sync and a pandera bridge: one consumer each, left to the community.
  • The extra check idea folded into the anomaly checks.

Changed from the earlier plan: the Lakeflow export is research with no version, pipeloom-dagster is placed in 1.4, and the two 1.0 follow-ups (parse-time budget tests, the Windows Airflow group) are placed in 1.4.

Risks:

  • Single maintainer. Nine minors at 2 to 4 weeks each is 4 to 8 months of full-time work, and every minor also releases every plugin in lockstep. Each release has a cut date, stretch items go first, and workspace-only demos are not in CI.
  • Narwhals may not cover anti join, is_duplicated and tz casts on its DuckDB backend. Spike this in week 1 of 1.1, confirm the supported backends in its docs, and override with SQL.
  • Dagster ownership. Prefect announced it is acquiring Dagster Labs (Market landscape), so the dagster API may shift. pipeloom-dagster uses only the public API and runs against a version matrix.
  • Airflow partition APIs arrived in 3.2 and may keep changing. They stay experimental and covered by the matrix.
  • Hash false positives (split checksums) and lineage overclaiming. Version the fingerprint, keep golden tests and completeness flags.
  • Wrong skips from --skip-unchanged. It is opt-in, anything unhashable forces a run, and every skip has a reason.
  • Windows. CI runs on windows-latest, and zoneinfo has no system timezone database there, process groups are POSIX-only, path guards differ, and DuckDB extension availability needs a check.
  • Supply chain. DuckDB extensions download binaries at runtime, the VS Code extension needs a separate release path and tokens, and the MCP SDK pulls a web stack. Each is isolated in its own distribution or job.
  • Data leaks through samples in PR comments, CI summaries and agent context. Defaults show counts only.
  • Prompt injection through artifact text in MCP, and DNS rebinding against the local UI. Both have the mitigations listed in 1.7.
  • External claims to verify first: the OpenLineage column facet status, UC external lineage GA, and PyIceberg write support. Each gets a verify-first task.
  • Duplicate OpenLineage events under Airflow. The rule (the provider emits inside Airflow, the sink everywhere else) needs a test.
  • WATCHER mode on shared storage. NFS attribute caching can hide fresh attempt files, so the sensor needs a bounded poll and a sentinel file (code PLA004, see the error codes).
  • Defer correctness. Reading production relations from a dev run needs read grants and the same schema. A missing relation must fail with a clear hint (code PLM204, see the error codes).

docs.title: 6. Decisions
docs.text:
Ordered by impact. All were decided on 2026-11-20; each item names the alternative it replaced.

  1. Dagster. Decided 2026-11-20: pipeloom-dagster ships as a plugin in 1.4, as the 1.0 roadmap promised. The alternative was a recipe over graph --units --output json and a plugin only with a co-maintainer.
  2. pipeloom ui. Decided 2026-11-20: it moves from 1.1 to 1.7.x and is built on the read layer. The alternatives were 1.2, or keeping 1.1.
  3. Version order. Decided 2026-11-20: DuckDB and the kit in 1.1, change intelligence in 1.2, intervals in 1.3. The alternatives put intervals or change intelligence first.
  4. on_schema_change. Decided 2026-11-20: deprecated in 1.5 in favor of schema_contract. It keeps working through 1.x and can be removed only in a new major. The alternative was keeping both.
  5. Interval ledger. Decided 2026-11-20: a reserved state key with document type pipeloom.intervals/1. The alternative was new optional StateStore methods, which stay the fallback named in 1.3.
  6. Interval writes. Decided 2026-11-20: an explicit replace_range field under the interval_writes capability. The alternative was reusing replace_partitions, which cannot guarantee range replacement.
  7. init default engine. Decided 2026-11-20: polars stays the default through 1.x, because changing a default is breaking under ADR-0016. DuckDB as the default waits for a new major, if one ever comes.
  8. Non-goal changes and the experimental tier. Decided 2026-11-20: all accepted as section 5 lists them (the three new non-goals, the Snowflake and UI rewording, the streaming note) together with the experimental tier and its lifecycle in section 3.
  9. Checksum inputs. Decided 2026-11-20: hash after ${var} resolution and before ${env} and ${secret}, so secrets never enter a hash. The alternative was hashing the unresolved text.
  10. pipeloom-duckdb. Decided 2026-11-20: in-tree and released in lockstep. The alternative was a separate repository as proof of the kit.
  11. OpenTelemetry attributes. Decided 2026-11-20: pipeloom.* plus the CI/CD semantic conventions where they fit. The alternative was pipeloom.* only.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: What problem or force makes a decision necessary. Facts only.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Option A. Pros and cons.
  • Option B. Pros and cons.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: What we chose, stated in full sentences.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: What becomes easier, what becomes harder, and what to revisit.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Proposed, Accepted, Deprecated, or Superseded by ADR-NNNN.

docs.title: Date
docs.text: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: ADR-0001: Record architecture decisions
docs.text: Architecture: Where the decision is recorded: docs/adr/ (this folder).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: pipeloom is designed before it is built, and plugin authors and contributors need to see why each choice was made, not only what it is. Decisions made in chat or in a pull request thread get lost. The architecture document (architecture.md) holds the full design, but a single long document is hard to amend one decision at a time.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Decisions only in the architecture document. One place to read. Changing one decision means editing a long page, and the reason a choice was made drifts away from its date.
  • A wiki or issue tracker. Easy to edit, but it lives outside the repository, so it is not versioned with the code and not reviewed in pull requests.
  • One ADR file per decision in docs/adr/. Versioned and reviewed with the code. Short files with a fixed shape. Needs a little discipline to keep the index current.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Record each significant decision as one ADR file in docs/adr/, named NNNN-short-slug.md, with the sections Context, Options, Decision, Consequences, Status and Date (see 0000-template.md). Numbers are never reused. A decision that changes gets a new ADR that supersedes the old one, and the old ADR's status changes to Superseded. README.md is the index.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Every decision has a stable link that issues, pull requests and docs can cite.
  • A new ADR goes through the same review as code.
  • The index must be updated with each new ADR.
  • ADR-0001 to ADR-0016 record the decisions of the initial design (2026-10-29).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0002: Engine abstraction: protocols plus Narwhals helpers
docs.text: Architecture: Section 5, Core protocols

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Moving from one engine to several couples code in the return type of a model, reads, schema, temporary views, writes, merge, metrics and catalog SQL. The core needs one contract that pandas, polars and PySpark plugins can all meet, without forcing Spark users into a lowest common denominator.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• (a) A hand-written protocol per plugin. Full control over IO, writes and metrics. More code per engine.
  • (b) Narwhals as the core abstraction. Small and dependency-free, but it has no write, SQL or catalog API, and only supports lazy PySpark.
  • (c) Ibis. Broad engine coverage, but heavy. Its write support is unverified, and it pushes users into an expression API.
  • (d) A hybrid. Hand-written protocols for the contract, Narwhals only for portable helpers.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Option (d).

  • The core contract is the hand-written protocols (Engine, EngineSession, Reader, Materializer, Catalog, MetricsProvider and others). Plugins own IO, writes, merge, catalogs, metrics and cancellation.
  • The core depends on Narwhals only for pipeloom.engine.portable. That module gives default count, filter_since, max_value, schema and evaluate that pandas, polars and PySpark plugins may reuse, through narwhals.stable.v2.
  • Model bodies receive native frames by default. frame_api: narwhals on a model passes Narwhals frames, so portable models work on any engine with capabilities.portable.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No lowest-common-denominator API for Spark users.
  • Engines can override the portable defaults for speed.
  • Narwhals stays a replaceable implementation detail. Pinning to stable.v2 limits API drift.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0003: Model authoring: YAML plus Python or SQL, declared inputs
docs.text: Architecture: Section 4, Configuration

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Declared dependencies (lesson L2) and YAML validation (L14) are core principles. Users still need a real transformation language.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• YAML only. Easy to validate, but too weak for transformations.
  • YAML plus Python. Full power, but SQL users must wrap queries in code.
  • YAML plus SQL. Familiar for SQL users, but no escape for logic SQL cannot express.
  • YAML plus both. Covers both audiences. Needs a rule for how inputs reach the body.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
YAML plus both. YAML declares every model. The body is either a Python callable or a SQL body. The inputs map binds local aliases to ref or source.

  • A Python callable is called as build(ctx, **inputs). Each alias becomes a keyword argument holding a relation.
  • SQL refers to aliases as table names. The engine registers them as named relations for that query only.
  • At compile time pipeloom imports nothing from the project. Validation layer L6 parses the callable's file with ast to check that the function exists and that its parameters equal ctx plus the input aliases.
  • Opt-in SQL table-reference checking through the sqlglot extra warns on mismatch.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Graphs are cheap to build, so Airflow can parse DAG files safely.
  • No Jinja templating.
  • Reads of undeclared tables through ctx.engine.native are a documented escape hatch outside lineage.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Superseded by ADR-0050.

docs.title: ADR-0004: Plugin discovery via entry points; eight groups
docs.text: Architecture: Section 6, Plugin system and plugin API version

docs.title: Context
docs.text: pipeloom needs engines, catalogs, state stores, sinks, secret providers, executors, renderers and naming strategies to be supplied by separately installed distributions, without the core importing them.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Entry points (stdlib importlib.metadata, the pytest model). No new dependency.
  • pluggy. Built for 1:N hook fan-out.
  • A dbt-style namespace import. Couples plugin layout to import paths.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Entry points. pipeloom picks one implementation per role by kind, which is 1-of-N selection, not hook fan-out, so pluggy adds a dependency without a matching need.

  • Eight groups: pipeloom.engines, pipeloom.catalogs, pipeloom.state_stores, pipeloom.sinks, pipeloom.secret_providers, pipeloom.executors, pipeloom.renderers, pipeloom.naming.
  • Each entry point resolves to a PluginSpec(name, kind, api_version, factory, config_model, compatible_engines).
  • Discovery reads metadata only. A plugin is imported only when a config names its kind. pipeloom plugins list imports nothing.
  • PIPELOOM_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 restricts loading to --plugin module:spec.
  • A duplicate kind within a group is error PLU002.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No extra dependency, and listing plugins is safe on locked-down hosts.
  • Plugins are versioned against the plugin API version (ADR-0016).
  • No hook fan-out. If a later feature needs it, this ADR must be revisited.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted. Amended by ADR-0017: the spec gains group, capabilities and description, built-ins come from an in-code table, and PLU003 is added.

docs.title: ADR-0005: Packaging
docs.text: Architecture: Section 17, ADR-0005 text

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The core and the engine, orchestrator and lineage integrations have different dependencies and release needs. Users should install only what they run.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• One distribution with extras. Its entry points are registered even when the extra's dependencies are missing, which leads to import errors at load. It also couples dependency bounds.
  • Separate distributions in separate repositories. High overhead.
  • Separate pipeloom-<plugin> distributions in one uv workspace.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The uv workspace.

  • The core is distribution pipeloom at the repo root. Plugins live in plugins/pipeloom-<name>/ with import package pipeloom_<name> (no namespace packages).
  • Convenience extras on pipeloom (for example pipeloom[polars]) just depend on the plugin distribution.
  • PyPI now: publish pipeloom 0.0.2 only. Plugin names are published with their first functional release, which avoids PEP 541 placeholder squatting.
  • Pending trusted publishers may be registered for the plugin names. Assumption: a pending publisher does not reserve a name (unverified).
  • [tool.uv.workspace] is added in 0.2 with the first plugin. Whether uv accepts an empty members glob is unverified.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One repository and one lockfile, with separate dependency bounds per plugin.
  • Plugin names stay unclaimed on PyPI until their first functional release, so someone else could register one in the meantime.
  • Lockstep versions apply during 0.x (ADR-0016).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted. Amended by ADR-0037 (the plugin is a package with an optional Airflow extra).

docs.title: ADR-0006: Ready-queue scheduler
docs.text: Architecture: Section 8, Execution and scheduler

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Running a graph level by level makes every unit in a level wait for the slowest one (lesson L6). Scheduling must be deterministic so runs are reproducible and testable.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Level barriers. Simple, but idle workers wait at each level.
  • A ready queue with no level barrier. Starts a unit as soon as its parents are done.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
A ready-queue scheduler with no level barrier.

  • When a unit reaches a terminal state, each child's count of pending parents goes down by one. A child whose count reaches zero is enqueued.
  • Ready units are ordered by descending count of downstream units, then by name, which is deterministic.
  • workers caps concurrency. pool tags (a later milestone) cap per-resource concurrency.
  • Policies: retries with exponential backoff and jitter (transient errors only unless retry_on: any), per-unit timeouts, cooperative cancellation with cancel_grace, skip-downstream by default with --fail-fast as an option, and a StateStore.lock concurrency guard per project and target.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Property tests (hypothesis) check the invariants: a unit starts only after all parents succeed, and every unit reaches exactly one terminal state.
  • Thread-executor timeouts are cooperative: code that ignores cancellation keeps running until the process ends. The process executor kills the child.
  • With boundary: task the orchestrator owns retries.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0007: Data handoff: execution units, inlining, intermediates
docs.text: Architecture: Section 8, ADR-0007

docs.title: Context
docs.text: With boundary: task, each unit runs in its own process or orchestrator task, so no in-memory or temporary-view handoff is possible (lesson L7).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Persisted intermediates everywhere. Simple, but costs IO.
  • Inlining everywhere. No extra IO, but recomputes shared work.
  • A hybrid, decided at compile time.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The hybrid.

  • ephemeral models are inlined. Their bodies run inside each consuming unit. Under boundary: process the result is memoized per run, so it is computed once.
  • intermediate models are persisted to <artifacts.root>/runs/<run_id>/intermediate/<model> (or a scratch schema the catalog provides). Finalize deletes them after intermediate_ttl.
  • view creates a catalog view where the engine supports it, never a session view.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The same plan runs in one process or many.
  • PLP406 warns when an ephemeral model fans out to more than ephemeral_fanout_warn (default 3) units and suggests intermediate.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0008: Incremental key, watermark state, strategies
docs.text: Architecture: Section 9, Incremental processing, write strategies, schema change

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Incremental logic must be declared, not inferred (lesson L12), and must survive crashes and orchestrator retries. Every write option must be applied by each strategy or rejected (L9).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Watermark kept in the target (max(column) of the target). No extra store, but needs the target to exist and read access to it.
  • Watermark in a StateStore with compare-and-swap. Works for targets that cannot be queried cheaply, at the cost of a store.
  • Both, selected per model with watermark_source: state | target.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
A declared key plus a lookback, with watermarks in a StateStore. watermark_source: target reads max(column) of the target instead.

  • Per unit: determine is_incremental, read the watermark w, filter the input with filter_since(input, column, w - lookback), write, then cas_watermark(expected=w, new=max_value(filtered input)). A CAS failure is PLM203.
  • State stores: sqlite (core, local), json (core, atomic rename), table (spark plugin). boundary: task requires table or json on a shared path.
  • Strategies: append, overwrite, replace_partitions, merge, scd2. Each returns a WriteResult.
  • Idempotency: each write receives token = "<run_id>:<model>". Engines without idempotent writes declare idempotent_writes=False.
  • on_schema_change: fail (default), ignore, append_new_columns, sync_all_columns.
  • Maintenance (optimize, vacuum, clustering) runs only from maintenance: blocks, never by default.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The watermark is committed after the write. A crash between the two reprocesses at most the lookback window plus the batch. That is safe for merge, overwrite and replace_partitions, and for append only when the engine has idempotent writes (otherwise PLC505 forbids retries).
  • A schema change under the default policy fails the unit (PLM202). Every detected change emits model.schema_changed.

docs.title: Amendment (0.9): SCD2
docs.text:
The scd2 strategy keeps a type 2 history of each unique_key.

  • No new config keys: unique_key, tracked_columns and the deletes block are reused, so manifests, checksums and plan hashes of projects without scd2 stay byte-identical. tracked_columns left unset means every business column except the unique_key columns and the deletes.column; an explicit empty list is PLP416.
  • System columns have fixed names: valid_from and valid_to (timestamp[us, UTC]) and is_current (boolean). A rename option can come later.
  • A change is detected by comparing the tracked columns directly, null-safely, with NaN counted as null. There is no row hash: it would depend on the engine and go stale when tracked_columns changes. A change in an untracked column is ignored.
  • valid_from and valid_to come from the run's start time (WriteConfig.run_started_at), the same on every retry of a run, so a re-run converges. Timestamps taken from a source column are a non-goal.
  • Deletes use the existing block with mode: hard only (soft is PLP416). A flagged row closes the key's current row; a flagged row for an unknown key is ignored. Keys missing from the batch are not closed. A closed key that comes back gets a new current row.
  • A null key, a key repeated in one batch, a batch column named like a system column, or an existing target without the system columns is PLM206 (WriteKeyError); the last one asks for --full-refresh.
  • The first load inserts every non-delete row as current. A full refresh drops the history and reloads as a first load: scd2 keeps its strategy under full refresh. A retry with the same token replays the stored result (ADR-0032); a re-run with an unchanged batch adds no versions.
  • Schema policy: scd2 keeps rows. The runner strips the system columns from the target schema before the policy, so the policy acts on business columns only.
  • A model contract (ADR-0044) describes the body output, so a system column there is PLP416. PLP416 also covers a unique_key, partition_by, cluster_by, deletes.column or tracked column that names a system column, and tracked columns that overlap the unique_key.
  • Counts reuse the WriteResult fields: rows_inserted is new current rows, rows_updated is rows closed by a change, rows_deleted is rows closed by a delete, rows_written is their sum.
  • WriteConfig gains tracked_columns (filled by the runner; empty only when the table has no business column besides the key and the delete column) and full_refresh, appended with defaults, and the engine types gain SCD2_COLUMNS. This is additive and stays within plugin API (0, 5).
  • Engines without scd2 get PLC501. The memory engine does not declare it; polars and pandas do (they share the filesystem write code, which rewrites the whole table on each scd2 write, like merge).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0009: Expectations and quarantine
docs.text: Architecture: Section 10, Data quality

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Data quality is a first-class feature (lesson L13). Rules need a clear action when a row or a dataset violates them, and failing rows should not vanish silently.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Fail-only checks. Simple, but one bad row stops the run.
  • DLT-style actions (warn, drop, fail) plus quarantine. Lets users choose per rule, and keeps dropped rows for inspection.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
DLT-style actions plus quarantine, evaluated after the transformation and before the write.

  • Row-level checks: not_null, accepted_values, range, regex, expr. Actions: warn, drop, fail.
  • Aggregate checks: unique, row_count, freshness. Actions: warn, fail. drop is PLP403.
  • EngineSession.evaluate computes every row-level predicate in one aggregate pass and returns per-expectation passed and failed counts. Unlike DLT, counts are kept on fail too.
  • drop filters rows that fail any drop predicate. If max_drop_ratio is exceeded, the unit fails with PLQ301.
  • With quality.quarantine: true, dropped rows go to <target>__quarantine with _pipeloom_run_id, _pipeloom_failed and _pipeloom_ts.
  • Lazy engines may cache the relation before the counting pass. The engine decides, and the decision is recorded in the metadata.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Results appear in run_results.json and in model.quality_evaluated events.
  • Expressions in expr checks use the engine's dialect and are not portable.
  • A quarantine table is extra storage that users must manage.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0010: Events, sinks, artifacts; rich for the console
docs.text: Architecture: Section 11, Events, logs and run metadata

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Logs, metrics, artifacts and lineage should not each have their own plumbing (lesson L1). Runs must also leave structured metadata that can be queried later.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Separate logging, metrics and lineage paths. Each is simple alone, but they drift apart.
  • One typed event stream with subscribers.
  • Console library: rich gives styled tables, colors and live progress in one dependency. structlog would still need a renderer for those. JSON lines need only the stdlib.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
One typed stream (pipeloom.event/1) and a synchronous in-process bus.

  • The envelope carries id, run_id, invocation_id, seq, ts, type, level, unit_id, model, attempt, data and context. Cross-invocation ordering is by (ts, invocation_id, seq).
  • The bus fans out to sinks in configured order. Each sink has a failure_budget (default 5 consecutive errors). When exhausted the sink is disabled and sink.disabled goes to the remaining sinks.
  • buffered: true wraps a sink in a bounded queue and worker thread, with drop-oldest and a count of drops.
  • A redaction filter masks registered secret values before any sink sees an event.
  • Built-in sinks: console, jsonl, file, artifacts (always on). pipeloom-openlineage maps units to OpenLineage jobs.
  • The console uses rich. JSON lines use the stdlib.
  • Artifacts: manifest.json (pipeloom.manifest/1) and run_results.json (pipeloom.run_results/1), with per-model and per-run metadata.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any consumer (console, files, lineage) is a sink, and tests can assert ordered events with RecordingSink.
  • A slow sink on the synchronous bus slows the run unless it is buffered.
  • JVM traces are trimmed on the console. The full trace goes to JSON events only.
  • The OpenLineage output-statistics facet is used if available (unverified).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted. Amended by ADR-0049: published artifact schemas.

docs.title: ADR-0011: Databricks job rendering
docs.text: Architecture: Section 12, The Databricks plugin

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A plan must run as one Databricks job, with run history, repair and the platform's own scheduling, and the same plan must also run locally.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• One task per unit as python_wheel_task, in a saved job. Gives run history, repair, only-subset runs and up to 1,000 tasks.
  • runs/submit (ephemeral). No saved job, but limited to 100 tasks and no repair history. Kept for --ephemeral dev runs.
  • Fewer, fused tasks. Needed only above the task limit (databricks.task_grouping).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Each unit becomes one python_wheel_task running pipeloom run --manifest ... --select unit:<id> --expect-plan-hash <h> --run-id ....

  • Task keys are sanitized model names, truncated with a short hash suffix (assumed 100-character limit, unverified).
  • Compute: serverless by default, with one environments[] entry pinning the pipeloom distributions to the running version (environment_version is an assumed field, unverified). compute: job_cluster is the alternative.
  • The default is a saved job found by tag pipeloom_job=<project>.<pipeline>.<target>: jobs/create, or reset when it exists, then run-now. Settings: max_concurrent_runs: 1, queueing, parameters pipeloom_run_id and full_refresh.
  • pipeloom databricks bundle writes a deterministic resources/pipeloom_<project>.job.yml. pipeloom databricks deploy uses the SDK directly.
  • An empty pipeloom_run_id resolves to dbx-<job.run_id>. Each task writes its unit file to artifacts.root and publishes taskValues (capped well under 48 KiB). A final pipeloom__finalize task (run_if: ALL_DONE) writes run_results.json.
  • Above 1,000 tasks the plan fails with PLD001 and a hint to use task grouping or split by selector. No automatic job chaining before 1.0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One job definition, whether it is triggered from the CLI, the Databricks UI or Airflow (ADR-0012).
  • Repair keeps the job run id, so the pipeloom run_id is stable and the attempt number increments.
  • pipeloom databricks run --select resolves to task keys plus finalize and uses only.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0012: Airflow rendering and modes
docs.text: Architecture: Section 13, The Airflow plugin

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Teams that orchestrate with Airflow need the pipeline graph as DAG tasks, with Airflow retries, assets and the same run identity as other orchestrators. Airflow DAG files are parsed often, so parsing must be safe and cheap.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
For the DATABRICKS mode:

  • (a) DatabricksWorkflowTaskGroup with DatabricksTaskOperator children. Builds the job spec from Airflow operators at parse time. That duplicates the pipeloom renderer, forces job name <dag_id>.<group_id>, fixes max_concurrent_runs=1, and disables "Repair All Failed Tasks" on Airflow 3.
  • (b) One run-now of the bundle-deployed job, with per-model status mirroring.

For the plugin overall: support Airflow 2 and 3, or Airflow 3 only.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Airflow 3 only (airflow.sdk, version >= 3.0). Dropping Airflow 2 support was accepted on 2026-10-29.

  • Load methods: MANIFEST (recommended) reads a precompiled manifest.json. PROJECT compiles YAML, which is safe because no user code runs (ADR-0003). Neither imports engines or connects to anything.
  • Modes: LOCAL, VIRTUALENV, KUBERNETES (wraps KubernetesPodOperator), DATABRICKS. DOCKER is later.
  • Shared behavior: one Airflow task per unit with Airflow owning retries, trigger rule all_success, a pipeloom_finalize task with all_done, and rid = af- plus 16 hex of sha256(dag_id + Airflow run_id), stable across task retries. With emit_assets, each model task declares Asset outlets.
  • DATABRICKS mode uses (b). A deferrable launch task finds or creates the job and calls run-now with pipeloom_run_id = rid, or repair if a failed run exists for rid. Each model gets a deferrable sensor that mirrors the state of its task_key.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One job definition however the run is triggered, and repair stays in Databricks.
  • Airflow task retries of a sensor only re-poll. Reruns go through launch.
  • Polling load is about one call per sensor per interval, with a configurable interval and an optional shared poll cache.
  • The shared artifact store for LOCAL and KUBERNETES modes is still open, with fsspec as the leading option (decide in 0.6).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted. Amended by ADR-0037: the floor is Airflow 3.2, the run id hashes NUL-separated parts, and the package has no hard Airflow dependency.

docs.title: ADR-0013: Run identity, idempotency, reruns
docs.text: Architecture: Section 17, ADR-0013 text

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A run can span several processes and orchestrator tasks, and tasks can be retried or repaired. Metadata, events and writes from all of them must join into one run, and a retry must not duplicate data.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• A fresh run_id per attempt. Simple, but splits one logical run into many.
  • A stable run_id with an attempt counter, derived deterministically by orchestrators.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• run_id is either caller-supplied or generated as YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-<6 hex>, matching [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}.
  • Orchestrators derive it deterministically: dbx-<job_run_id> or af-<hash>.
  • Orchestrator retries and repairs keep the run_id and increment the attempt.
  • Local pipeloom retry --from <run_id> creates a new run with parent_run_id that runs the failed, skipped and cancelled units of the parent (see the 0.8 amendment).
  • Writes are idempotent through the token <run_id>:<model>.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A cleared-and-rerun Airflow task continues the same pipeloom run.
  • Engines without idempotent writes declare idempotent_writes=False, and validation forbids retries on non-idempotent append (PLC505).
  • Run records go to the state store for history.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted. Amended in 0.8 (pipeloom retry).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• pipeloom retry --from RUN_ID runs the units that run RUN_ID did not finish, in a new run. The parent is the folder <artifacts root>/runs/RUN_ID of the bound target. It is read with the --state reference loader of ADR-0042: its manifest.json and run_results.json.
  • The selection is result:fail, result:skip and result:cancelled, only for the values that occur in the parent's rows, against a reference built from the parent folder. It is deliberately not result:fail+: the + follows the current graph and would pull in descendants the parent never selected, for example when the parent ran with --select. The rows of the parent already say what it selected, so the failed units and the descendants that were skipped because of them are exactly the set to run again. A parent with none of the three has nothing to retry: the command prints run <id> has nothing to retry and exits 0 without a run folder.
  • The retry also selects every intermediate model that a retried unit reads, directly or through other intermediate models, even when the parent built it. An intermediate model lives under the folder of the run that built it, so the retry cannot read the parent's copy; it builds its own, which is safe because an intermediate model always overwrites.
  • Inherited defer never defers a model whose row in the parent is succeeded. Such a model is unselected in the retry and would otherwise be read from the reference, so the retry would build on production upstreams instead of what the parent built in this target. Those models are read from this target (RunOptions.not_deferred).
  • The vars are read before the project loads, so a model that needs ${var:x} loads with the parent's vars. The parent folder is found under the target's artifacts root, or under <project dir>/target when the project cannot bind yet. If the parent cannot be found and the project fails to load, the load errors stay, with a hint to pass the vars with --vars.
  • The command takes no --select, --exclude, --manifest, --expect-plan-hash, --run-started-at, --state or --defer. It inherits from the parent: the vars of its manifest (--vars on top), full_refresh (an explicit --full-refresh or --no-full-refresh wins), and state and defer from the args of its run_results.json. Select and exclude are not inherited.
  • The project is compiled fresh, so a fixed model is the point of the retry. A plan hash that differs from the parent's is expected and is not checked.
  • The retry gets its own run id (generated, or --run-id, which must differ from --from) and records the parent as parent_run_id in run_results.json, the state store record and the run.started event. Reusing the id of a retry continues that retry and keeps its parent.
  • A parent that has no run_results.json (it never existed, never finished or is still running), that belongs to another project or that ran another target is PLX113. A parent that is still running and holds the run lock gets PLX105 from the normal lock path.

docs.title: Risk
docs.text: A unit can fail after its write committed (PLM203). The retry runs under a new run id, so the idempotency token <run_id>:<model> is new and an append writes the rows again. Retries that must not duplicate keep the original run id instead (run again with --run-id set to the parent's id, which continues that run and replays tokens).

docs.title: ADR-0014: Secrets by reference
docs.text: Architecture: Section 14, Security and secrets

docs.title: Context
docs.text: YAML files, manifests, events and artifacts are committed, logged and shared. Secret values must never end up in them.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Literal secrets in YAML. Convenient, and unsafe.
  • Environment variables only. Safe, but no integration with platform secret stores.
  • References resolved at runtime through providers.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Secrets by reference.

  • Fields whose names match secret patterns accept only ${secret:...} or ${env:...}. A literal is PLS104.
  • ${secret:<provider>/<path>} resolves at runtime inside the executing process through the pipeloom.secret_providers group. Providers: env and file (core, mode-checked), databricks (secret scopes), airflow (connections and variables).
  • The manifest, events and artifacts store only the references. Resolved values are registered with the redaction filter (ADR-0010).
  • Discovery never imports plugins until a config names them. PIPELOOM_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD exists for locked-down hosts.
  • Grants are declared in YAML and applied by the catalog. pipeloom never escalates privileges.
  • Supply chain: trusted publishing (OIDC) with PEP 740 attestations, actions pinned by commit SHA, no pull_request_target workflows, integration secrets only in protected environments, and private vulnerability reporting through SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The compile-time manifest is safe to share. Secrets exist only in the running process.
  • ${secret:...} is not resolved at compile time, so a bad reference shows up at run time (or in --preflight).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0015: Python 3.11 or newer; click CLI; pydantic v2; hatchling; mypy strict
docs.text: Architecture: Section 17, ADR-0015 text, and section 18

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A new public project started in late 2026 must pick a Python floor and a base toolchain. Python 3.10 reaches end of life in October 2026.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Python floor: 3.10 (reaches end of life in October 2026) or 3.11.
  • CLI: click (click>=8.2, for CliRunner to expose result.stderr; the 0.0.2 skeleton depended on click>=8.1).
  • Config models: pydantic v2, which also exports the JSON Schema (section 4).
  • Build backend: hatchling.
  • Types: mypy in strict mode.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Python 3.11 or newer, click for the CLI, pydantic v2 for config models, hatchling as the build backend, and mypy --strict in CI. CI runs Python 3.11 to 3.14 on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Code may use 3.11 features, and users on 3.10 cannot install pipeloom.
  • The package had one runtime dependency (click) at 0.0.2. From 0.1 the CLI needs click>=8.2, and the runtime also depends on pydantic>=2.12 and PyYAML>=6.0.2.
  • pyproject.toml and CI follow this ADR.
  • While the repo was private, CI ran one Windows and one macOS job on 3.12 only, to save macOS minutes. The full matrix returned when the repo went public on 2026-11-02.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0016: Versioning, release, plugin API version
docs.text: Architecture: Section 15 (Release) and section 6 (Plugin API version)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Several distributions ship from one repository, and several contracts evolve at different speeds: the package, the plugin protocol, the config format and the manifest, event and run_results schemas.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Lockstep versions for first-party distributions during 0.x, with one tag. Simple releases. Plugin-only fixes still bump every distribution.
  • Independent versions per distribution. Precise, but more release work and a larger compatibility matrix while the API is moving.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• SemVer per distribution, with lockstep versions for first-party distributions during 0.x and one tag vX.Y.Z.
  • The tag workflow checks that the tag equals the version, builds, then publishes to PyPI by trusted publishing, then creates the GitHub release with notes from CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog).
  • Each distribution publishes from its own job and its own GitHub environment: pypi for the core and pypi-<plugin> for each plugin (pypi-polars, pypi-pandas, pypi-spark, pypi-databricks, pypi-airflow). PyPI accepts only one pending trusted publisher per owner, repository, workflow and environment, so new plugin projects cannot share one environment. Amended on 2026-11-04 after PyPI rejected a second pending publisher for pypi; ADR-0023 has the job layout.
  • config_version, the manifest and event schema versions, and the plugin API version are versioned separately.
  • pipeloom.plugins.API_VERSION = (MAJOR, MINOR), independent of the package version. MINOR covers additive changes. MAJOR covers breaking protocol changes. The core accepts plugins with the same MAJOR and MINOR not above its own, otherwise it raises PLU001.
  • Before 1.0 the plugin API is 0.x and any minor may break. Plugin API 1.0 ships with pipeloom 1.0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Plugin authors can target a plugin API version instead of a package version.
  • Lockstep versioning means plugin-only fixes bump every distribution during 0.x.
  • At 1.0, config_version: 1, the plugin API 1.0, and the manifest, event and run_results schemas v1 are declared stable.

docs.title: Amendment (1.0): stability and deprecation policy
docs.text: From 1.0.0 pipeloom follows Semantic Versioning for the surfaces below. The user-facing summary is Stability and deprecations.

docs.title: What is stable
docs.text:
• CLI command names, flag names and their meanings, and the exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 130.
  • Every JSON output that carries a version tag.
  • config_version: 1. It is the only value accepted through 1.x.
  • The artifact schemas pipeloom.manifest/1, pipeloom.run_results/1, pipeloom.event/1, pipeloom.unit_states/1 and pipeloom.unit_graph/1, and the event types, as defined in ADR-0049.
  • Plugin API 1.0: the protocols, PluginSpec and the capabilities. pipeloom.testing is part of the plugin API.
  • The meaning of each diagnostic code. Messages and hints are not stable.
  • The documented Python API: the pipeloom top-level exports and pipeloom.api.

Not stable: console text (including log lines and table layout) and anything undocumented, such as private modules and names that start with an underscore.

docs.title: What counts as breaking
docs.text:
A breaking change needs a new major version. These are breaking:

  • Removing or renaming anything listed above.
  • Changing a type, a default or an exit code.
  • Adding a value to a closed enum.
  • Adding a required method to a plugin protocol.
  • Raising a warning to an error.
