To add cells of your own, subclass EngineContract in a test module and override engine_factory, as the in-tree plugins do. That entry point keeps working beside the plugin. StateStoreContract is the equivalent suite for state stores, subclassed the same way.

docs.title: Run artifacts
docs.text: A run writes its files under the artifacts root, target by default (set it with artifacts.root on the target). Paths in artifacts are POSIX.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
target/
  manifest.json            copy of the latest run's manifest
  run_results.json         copy of the latest run's results
  runs/<run_id>/
    manifest.json          the plan that ran (pipeloom.manifest/1)
    run_results.json       the outcome of the run (pipeloom.run_results/1)
    events/<invocation_id>.jsonl   events of each invocation
    units/<unit_id>/attempt-<n>.json   one file per attempt of a unit
    logs/<unit_id>-attempt-<n>.log     output of a task-boundary unit
    intermediate/<model>/          result of an `intermediate` model, deleted after `artifacts.intermediate_ttl`

Finalize writes run_results.json into the run folder, then copies it and the manifest to the root. The run folder is the source of truth; the root copies are for convenience.

Finalize also deletes the intermediate/ folder of other runs once they are idle. A finished run is judged by the intermediate_ttl it recorded. A run with no run_results.json, or whose manifest is newer than its results (resumed, then possibly crashed again), is judged by the newest modification time under its run folder and expires after max(ttl, 1h) of inactivity, so an active run is never deleted.

docs.title: Attempt files
docs.text: Each unit writes units/<unit_id>/attempt-<n>.json when the attempt ends, whatever the outcome. The file holds one results row, the same object that appears in run_results.json. The runner writes it, so it exists for a unit that ran in a child process too. A reused run id keeps counting: the next attempt is one above the highest file. A unit that started under boundary: task and left no attempt file is reported as failed with PLX106, with the end of its log as the excerpt.

docs.title: run_results.json
docs.text:
schema is pipeloom.run_results/1. Top-level keys:

Key Content schema The schema name and version. metadata pipeloom_version, generated_at, invocation_id, plugins. args The options of the invocation: select, exclude, manifest, run_id, full_refresh, fail_fast, workers, boundary, lock. run One object for the whole run, below. results One row per persisted model, sorted by unit_id.

run holds run_id, parent_run_id (null, or the run pipeloom retry --from retried), invocation_ids (every invocation that worked on the run), project, target, plan_hash, selector, full_refresh, status (succeeded, failed or cancelled), started_at, ended_at, duration_ms, counts (total and one number per unit status), totals (rows_written and bytes_written of succeeded units), identity (user, host, orchestrator, orchestrator_ids), pipeloom_version, plugins, python_version, git_sha (null outside a git repository), exit_code, intermediate_ttl (seconds; the TTL this run was finalized with, which other runs use to judge its intermediates) and warnings (run-level messages, such as intermediate_cleanup_failed: <run_id>: <error> when an expired folder could not be deleted).

Every row in results has every key. Ephemeral models have no row: they appear in the ephemeral_inlined list of the units that inline them.

Field Meaning unique_id, unit_id Model id (model.<project>.<name>) and execution unit id. ephemeral_inlined Ephemeral models computed inside this unit. materialization, strategy, relation_name What was built and where. status succeeded, failed, skipped or cancelled. skip_reason upstream_failed or fail_fast for a skipped unit; not_run (or the orchestrator's own reason) when pipeloom finalize found no result; else null. attempt, retries_used Attempt number; retries are 0 in 0.2. started_at, ended_at, duration_ms, queue_wait_ms Timing. Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC. rows_read Rows read per input alias; null where the engine is lazy (polars). rows_written, rows_inserted, bytes_written Write metrics; null when the engine does not report them. full_refresh, is_incremental Whether the unit was rebuilt from scratch; incremental is false in 0.2. schema_hash sha256 of the canonical output schema (name, dtype, nullable, in column order). error Null, or code, category (transient or permanent), message, hint, exception_type, trace_excerpt. engine, engine_version, executor What ran the unit (thread or process). idempotency_token <run_id>:<unit_id>.

Incremental and merge models fill rows_updated, rows_deleted, target_version, is_incremental, watermark_before and watermark_after (ISO text for dates and timestamps), and warnings carries watermark_seeded: target when the state store had no watermark. Fields that later versions fill stay null or empty: rows_dropped, rows_quarantined, bytes_read, schema_changes and expectations. orchestrator_ids holds the ids from --orchestrator-id.

docs.title: JSON Schemas
docs.text:
Each document names its schema in a schema property, and each schema is published next to the config schemas (ADR-0049):

Document Schema manifest.json (pipeloom.manifest/1) manifest.json run_results.json (pipeloom.run_results/1) run_results.json an attempt file #/$defs/result of run_results.json one event (pipeloom.event/1) event.json --unit-states (pipeloom.unit_states/1) unit_states.json graph --units --output json (pipeloom.unit_graph/1) unit_graph.json

A field added after 1.0 is optional in the schema, so 1.0 documents keep validating; the 1.0 required sets are frozen, and CI validates frozen 1.0 documents against the current schemas and current output against the frozen 1.0 schemas.

Compatibility within a version: consumers must ignore fields they do not know, since the schemas leave objects open. A 1.x release may add optional fields, new event types and new skip reasons and stays on /1: skip reasons are open strings both in the row skip_reason and in the unit.skipped event. Every other enumerated value is closed: status of a row, of the run, of run.completed and of a unit state, the event level, the error category (transient or permanent), unit.cancelled reason, model.input_read kind, model.schema_changed action, run.started boundary, state.watermark_committed source and model.log level. A new value of one of them, or any change a consumer must understand, moves the document to /2.

docs.title: Unit graph
docs.text:
pipeloom graph --units --output json prints the execution units an orchestrator runs one by one, tagged pipeloom.unit_graph/1. With --manifest PATH it reads the plan from that manifest, so plan_hash is the manifest's; without it the command compiles the project. A unit is in scope when its persisted model is selected; parents and edges only name units in scope.

Key Meaning project, target, plan_hash From the plan. selectors select and exclude as given; the finalize command repeats them. finalize has no --state, so when a selector uses state: or result: it gets --select unit:<id> for each unit instead. placeholders project_dir, manifest and run_id: written as {name} in every argv. units Topological order, ties broken by unit id. Each has unit_id, unique_id, nodes, materialized, relation (catalog, schema, name) and relation_name (null without a relation), assets, parents, tags, retries, retry_delay_s, retry_on, timeout_s and argv. edges {"from": parent, "to": child}. finalize.argv The command line that closes the run.

An argv starts with pipeloom; the unit id, target and plan hash are literal, and every --plugin given to graph is repeated at the end, so each process can load the same kinds. Assets are pipeloom://{project}/{target}/{relation_name} with each part percent-encoded; intermediates and models without a relation have none. The schema is unit_graph.json.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: events/<invocation_id>.jsonl holds the events of one invocation, one JSON object per line. An invocation that runs a single unit writes only its own file; the owning invocation forwards the unit events it receives, keeping the original invocation id and sequence number. Order events across files by (ts, invocation_id, seq).

docs.title: Where each command is explained
docs.text:
The generated reference at the end of this page lists every flag. These pages explain what the commands are for. A test keeps this table in step with the commands.

Command Explained in pipeloom init pipeloom init, Quickstart pipeloom demo pipeloom demo, Quickstart pipeloom new pipeloom new model pipeloom new model pipeloom new model, Quickstart pipeloom validate Inspecting a project, Quickstart pipeloom compile Inspecting a project, Selection by state pipeloom ls Inspecting a project pipeloom graph Inspecting a project, Orchestrator protocol pipeloom run Running a pipeline pipeloom retry Retrying a run pipeloom test Testing models pipeloom build Testing models pipeloom runs Run history pipeloom runs ls Run history pipeloom runs show Run history pipeloom finalize Closing the run, Orchestrator protocol pipeloom docs Docs site pipeloom docs generate Docs site pipeloom docs serve Docs site pipeloom schema JSON Schema pipeloom schema export JSON Schema pipeloom explain Running a pipeline pipeloom plugins Inspecting a project pipeloom plugins list Inspecting a project pipeloom databricks Databricks plugin, Databricks commands pipeloom databricks bundle Bundle and direct deploy pipeloom databricks deploy Bundle and direct deploy pipeloom databricks run Run pipeloom databricks repair Repair

docs.title: pipeloom init
docs.text:
pipeloom init [DIRECTORY] creates a project, like dbt init. DIRECTORY defaults to a new folder named after the project in the current directory.

  • When stdin is a terminal it asks for what the flags leave out: the project name (default: the directory name), the engine (polars, pandas, spark, databricks or duckdb, default polars; the default stays polars) and, on databricks, the Unity Catalog catalog (default main). Otherwise, or with --no-input, it uses the flags and those defaults.
  • Each layer folder, models/bronze, models/silver and models/gold, gets one .py file with a decorated model. polars, spark and databricks models return ctx.sql(...); pandas models are frame code, since pandas has no SQL. pipeloom.yml holds the source group raw and a models: tree that sets each layer's schema and tags; models/silver/_properties.yml holds a description. .vscode/settings.json maps project.json to pipeloom.yml and properties.json to models/**/*.yml. polars, pandas and spark read a small CSV in data/, so pipeloom run works right away on polars and pandas. databricks reads samples.tpch.orders and comes with a state table, an artifacts volume and a serverless deploy block; the comments in pipeloom.yml say what to create before pipeloom databricks deploy.
  • A directory that is not empty needs --force. Existing files are never overwritten: they are kept and listed as skipped. A directory that already holds pipeloom.yml is refused.
  • Exit codes: 0 on success, 2 on a usage error (bad name or engine, --catalog without databricks, an existing project, a non-empty directory without --force).

docs.title: pipeloom demo
docs.text:
pipeloom demo [DIRECTORY] is the quickest way to see pipeloom work. It writes the init project for the duckdb engine into DIRECTORY (default pipeloom_demo in the current directory), runs pipeloom build on it (a unit test, three models and their data tests), writes the docs site and prints where it is and what to try next.

  • It needs the DuckDB engine (pip install "pipeloom[duckdb]"). Without it the command stops with PLU004 and the install command as the hint. It never falls back to another engine, so the demo is the same on every machine.
  • DIRECTORY must be missing or empty. The site is DIRECTORY/target/docs/index.html.
  • Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 when the engine is missing or the build fails, 2 for a directory that is not empty.

docs.title: pipeloom new model
docs.text:
pipeloom new model NAME adds one model file to a project and prints its path.

  • The file is models/<folder>/<NAME>.py, with one function NAME decorated with @model. --folder is relative to the first model path and cannot leave it.
  • --sql writes a body that returns ctx.sql("select 1 as id"). --python writes a frame stub that raises NotImplementedError until you write the body. Without a flag, pandas default targets get --python and the rest --sql. Add one parameter per input, named like the model or source table it reads.
  • Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 when the project does not load, 2 on a usage error (bad name, a Python keyword or ctx, model or ModelContext as the name, a model or file that exists, --sql with --python, a folder outside the model path, a file outside every python_paths root, or a name that is already a folder where the file would go, such as bronze in an init project).

docs.title: pipeloom
docs.text:
pipeloom: engine-agnostic data pipelines, with models written as Python functions.

Usage:

pipeloom [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

  --version  Show the version and exit.
  --help     Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom build
docs.text:
Run the unit tests of the selected models, then run them with data tests.

Any failed unit test stops the build with exit 1 before a run id exists and before any write. Each model's data tests then run after its write; a failed one (PLQ303) fails the unit, skips its descendants and leaves the data written. Takes the flags of run. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a unit test, a unit or a check failed, 2 bad usage, 130 stopped.

Usage:

pipeloom build [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --project-dir DIRECTORY      Directory that holds pipeloom.yml.  [default:
                               .]
  --vars TEXT                  Variables as a YAML or JSON mapping; they
                               override the vars block.
  --target TEXT                Target to bind; default_target or the only
                               target when omitted.
  --plugin MODULE:ATTR         A PluginSpec to load besides the installed
                               plugins. Repeatable.
  -s, --select SELECTOR        Models to include: name, tag:x, path:dir,
                               materialized:x, +model, model+, N+model,
                               model+N. Space unions, comma intersects.
                               Repeatable, all are unioned.
  --exclude SELECTOR           Remove the models this selector matches from
                               the selection. Repeatable.
  --state DIR                  Folder of a reference manifest.json (and
                               optionally run_results.json), for the state:
                               and result: selectors. Relative to the project
                               dir unless absolute. `compile --stable` or the
                               artifacts root (target) both work.
  --defer                      Read the parents this run does not select from
                               the relations of the --state manifest instead
                               of this target's, so a dev run of one model
                               reads the production tables. Needs --state.
                               Refused for unit invocations and the task
                               boundary (PLX111).
  --log-format [text|json]     Diagnostics and events on stderr: readable text
                               or one JSON object per line.  [default: text]
  --manifest FILE              Run the plan of this manifest instead of
                               compiling the project.
  --expect-plan-hash HEX       Stop with PLX103 unless the plan hash is this
                               sha256.
  --run-id TEXT                Name of the run. Reusing it continues that run.
                               Default: a timestamp and a suffix.
  --full-refresh BOOLEAN       Rebuild append tables from scratch. Takes an
                               optional true or false.  [default: False]
  --run-started-at ISO8601     Start time of the run, with a UTC offset (for
                               example the start of the orchestrator job).
                               Engines use it to make writes idempotent. Needs
                               --run-id. A reused run id keeps the start it
                               recorded.
  --orchestrator-id KEY=VALUE  An id the orchestrator gave this run, such as
                               job_run_id=42. It goes into the attempt files,
                               the run results and the context of every event.
                               Repeatable; a later duplicate wins. Key:
                               [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}; value: 1 to 256 printable
                               characters.
  --fail-fast                  After the first failure, start no more units.
  --no-lock                    Do not take the run lock.
  --workers INTEGER RANGE      Units to run at once. Default: the target's
                               setting, else min(4, CPUs).  [x>=1]
  --boundary [process|task]    process runs units on threads here; task runs
                               each in its own process. Default: the target's
                               boundary.
  --warn-error                 Exit 1 on warnings too.
  --cancel-grace DURATION      After a stop request (Ctrl+C, SIGTERM) or a
                               timeout, how long running units may finish
                               before they are killed, as 30s, 2m or 30.
                               Default: the setting, else 30s.
  --help                       Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom compile-
docs.text:
Validate the project and write the plan to a manifest file.

Usage:

pipeloom compile- [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --project-dir DIRECTORY    Directory that holds pipeloom.yml.  [default: .]
  --vars TEXT                Variables as a YAML or JSON mapping; they
                             override the vars block.
  --target TEXT              Target to bind; default_target or the only target
                             when omitted.
  --plugin MODULE:ATTR       A PluginSpec to load besides the installed
                             plugins. Repeatable.
  -s, --select SELECTOR      Models to include: name, tag:x, path:dir,
                             materialized:x, +model, model+, N+model, model+N.
                             Space unions, comma intersects. Repeatable, all
                             are unioned.
  --exclude SELECTOR         Remove the models this selector matches from the
                             selection. Repeatable.
  --state DIR                Folder of a reference manifest.json (and
                             optionally run_results.json), for the state: and
                             result: selectors. Relative to the project dir
                             unless absolute. `compile --stable` or the
                             artifacts root (target) both work.
  --log-format [text|json]   Diagnostics and events on stderr: readable text
                             or one JSON object per line.  [default: text]
  --boundary [process|task]  Where units run; default is the target's boundary
                             (process).
  --out PATH                 Manifest file, relative to the project dir unless
                             absolute.  [default: target/manifest.json]
  --stable                   Blank generated_at, invocation_id and the
                             selection so the same project and target always
                             give the same bytes. `run --manifest` then runs
                             every model unless --select or --exclude is
                             given.
  --warn-error               Exit 1 on warnings too.
  --help                     Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom demo
docs.text:
Create a sample project on DuckDB in DIRECTORY, build it and write its docs site.

DIRECTORY defaults to a new folder named pipeloom_demo and must be empty or missing (exit 2 otherwise). Needs the DuckDB engine: pip install "pipeloom[duckdb]"; without it the command stops with PLU004 (exit 1). It never falls back to another engine.

Usage:

pipeloom demo [OPTIONS] [DIRECTORY]

Options:

  --log-format [text|json]  Diagnostics and events on stderr: readable text or
                            one JSON object per line.  [default: text]
  --help                    Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom docs
docs.text:
Build and serve the docs site (one HTML file, read only).

Usage:

pipeloom docs [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:

  --help  Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom docs generate
docs.text:
Write index.html: the graph, every model and source, and the last run's results.

Usage:

pipeloom docs generate [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --project-dir DIRECTORY   Directory that holds pipeloom.yml.  [default: .]
  --vars TEXT               Variables as a YAML or JSON mapping; they override
                            the vars block.
  --target TEXT             Target to bind; default_target or the only target
                            when omitted.
  --plugin MODULE:ATTR      A PluginSpec to load besides the installed
                            plugins. Repeatable.
  --log-format [text|json]  Diagnostics and events on stderr: readable text or
                            one JSON object per line.  [default: text]
  --out PATH                Output folder, relative to the project dir unless
                            absolute. Default: target/docs.
  --manifest FILE           Render this manifest instead of compiling the
                            project.
  --run-results FILE        A run_results.json to show. Default: the one at

  --help                    Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom docs serve
docs.text:
Serve the generated site until Ctrl+C, rebuilding it when the models change. It never opens a browser.

Usage:

pipeloom docs serve [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --project-dir DIRECTORY  Directory that holds pipeloom.yml.  [default: .]
  --vars TEXT              Variables as a YAML or JSON mapping; they override
                           the vars block.
  --target TEXT            Target to bind; default_target or the only target
                           when omitted.
  --plugin MODULE:ATTR     A PluginSpec to load besides the installed plugins.
                           Repeatable.
  --dir PATH               Folder to serve, relative to the project dir unless
                           absolute. Default: target/docs.
  --host TEXT              Address to listen on.  [default: 127.0.0.1]
  --port INTEGER RANGE     Port to use.  [default: 8000; 0<=x<=65535]
  --help                   Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom explain
docs.text:
Print what a diagnostic CODE means, for example PLX101 (case-insensitive).

Shows the title, layer, severity, status, the version the code appeared in, the explanation and the link to the error-code page. Reads no project.

Usage:

pipeloom explain [OPTIONS] CODE

Options:

  --help  Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom finalize
docs.text:
Merge the unit results of a run into run_results.json and close the run.

Units in scope (default: the whole plan) take their attempt file, else the state given with --unit-states or --unit-states-json, else they are skipped as not_run, which does not fail the run. A unit marked excluded gets no row. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a unit failed, 2 bad usage, 130 cancelled. Running it again rewrites the same results.

Usage:

pipeloom finalize [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --project-dir DIRECTORY      Directory that holds pipeloom.yml.  [default:
                               .]
  --vars TEXT                  Variables as a YAML or JSON mapping; they
                               override the vars block.
  --target TEXT                Target to bind; default_target or the only
                               target when omitted.
  --plugin MODULE:ATTR         A PluginSpec to load besides the installed
                               plugins. Repeatable.
  -s, --select SELECTOR        Models to include: name, tag:x, path:dir,
                               materialized:x, +model, model+, N+model,
                               model+N. Space unions, comma intersects.
                               Repeatable, all are unioned.
  --exclude SELECTOR           Remove the models this selector matches from
                               the selection. Repeatable.
  --log-format [text|json]     Diagnostics and events on stderr: readable text
                               or one JSON object per line.  [default: text]
  --run-id TEXT                The run to close: the run id every unit
                               invocation used.  [required]
  --manifest FILE              Use the plan of this manifest instead of
                               compiling the project.
  --expect-plan-hash HEX       Stop with PLX103 unless the plan hash is this
                               sha256.
  --unit-states PATH           A JSON file, schema pipeloom.unit_states/1,
                               with what the orchestrator knows about units
                               that wrote no attempt file: {unit_id: {status:
                               skipped|cancelled|failed|excluded, reason,
                               code, message, orchestrator_ids}}.
  --unit-states-json TEXT      The same document as --unit-states, given
                               inline (for an orchestrator that cannot share a
                               file). Not together with --unit-states.
  --orchestrator-id KEY=VALUE  An id the orchestrator gave this run, such as
                               job_run_id=42. It goes into the attempt files,
                               the run results and the context of every event.
                               Repeatable; a later duplicate wins. Key:
                               [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}; value: 1 to 256 printable
                               characters.
  --run-started-at ISO8601     Start time of the run, with a UTC offset. A run
                               that recorded its start keeps it.
  --help                       Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom graph
docs.text:
Print the graph of the selected models, in dependency order.

With --units --output json, print the selected execution units instead, for an orchestrator that runs them one by one.

Usage:

pipeloom graph [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --project-dir DIRECTORY         Directory that holds pipeloom.yml.
                                  [default: .]
  --vars TEXT                     Variables as a YAML or JSON mapping; they
                                  override the vars block.
  --target TEXT                   Target to bind; default_target or the only
                                  target when omitted.
  --plugin MODULE:ATTR            A PluginSpec to load besides the installed
                                  plugins. Repeatable.
  -s, --select SELECTOR           Models to include: name, tag:x, path:dir,
                                  materialized:x, +model, model+, N+model,
                                  model+N. Space unions, comma intersects.
                                  Repeatable, all are unioned.
  --exclude SELECTOR              Remove the models this selector matches from
                                  the selection. Repeatable.
  --state DIR                     Folder of a reference manifest.json (and
                                  optionally run_results.json), for the state:
                                  and result: selectors. Relative to the
                                  project dir unless absolute. `compile
                                  --stable` or the artifacts root (target)
                                  both work.
  --log-format [text|json]        Diagnostics and events on stderr: readable
                                  text or one JSON object per line.  [default:
                                  text]
  --output [text|dot|mermaid|json]
                                  Format of the graph: text (name <- parents),
                                  Graphviz dot, Mermaid or JSON. --units needs
                                  json.  [default: text]
  --units                         Print the execution units of the plan
                                  instead of the models, with the command line
                                  that runs each and the one that finalizes
                                  the run (schema pipeloom.unit_graph/1).
                                  Needs --output json.
  --manifest FILE                 With --units: read the plan from this
                                  manifest instead of compiling the project,
                                  so plan_hash is the manifest's.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom init
docs.text:
Create a project in DIRECTORY (default: a new folder named after the project).

docs.title: pipeloom retry
docs.text:
Run again what a finished run did not finish. Exit codes as run; 1 also for PLX113.

Selects the units of run RUN_ID that failed, timed out, were skipped or were cancelled, and runs them in a new run that records RUN_ID as its parent. The project is compiled again, so a fixed model is picked up. The retry inherits the vars (--vars wins), --full-refresh, --state and --defer of the run it retries.

Usage:

pipeloom retry [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --project-dir DIRECTORY         Directory that holds pipeloom.yml.
                                  [default: .]
  --vars TEXT                     Variables as a YAML or JSON mapping; they
                                  override the vars block.
  --target TEXT                   Target to bind; default_target or the only
                                  target when omitted.
  --plugin MODULE:ATTR            A PluginSpec to load besides the installed
                                  plugins. Repeatable.
  --log-format [text|json]        Diagnostics and events on stderr: readable
                                  text or one JSON object per line.  [default:
                                  text]
  --from RUN_ID                   The finished run to retry: its failed,
                                  skipped and cancelled units run again.
                                  [required]
  --run-id TEXT                   Name of the new run; it must differ from
                                  --from. Default: a timestamp and a suffix.
  --full-refresh / --no-full-refresh
                                  Rebuild append tables from scratch. Default:
                                  what the retried run did.
  --orchestrator-id KEY=VALUE     An id the orchestrator gave this run, such
                                  as job_run_id=42. It goes into the attempt
                                  files, the run results and the context of
                                  every event. Repeatable; a later duplicate
                                  wins. Key: [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}; value: 1 to
                                  256 printable characters.
  --fail-fast                     After the first failure, start no more
                                  units.
  --no-lock                       Do not take the run lock.
  --workers INTEGER RANGE         Units to run at once. Default: the target's
                                  setting, else min(4, CPUs).  [x>=1]
  --boundary [process|task]       process runs units on threads here; task
                                  runs each in its own process. Default: the
                                  target's boundary.
  --warn-error                    Exit 1 on warnings too.
  --cancel-grace DURATION         After a stop request (Ctrl+C, SIGTERM) or a
                                  timeout, how long running units may finish
                                  before they are killed, as 30s, 2m or 30.
                                  Default: the setting, else 30s.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.

docs.title: pipeloom run
docs.text:
Run the selected models. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a unit or a check failed, 2 bad usage, 130 stopped.

The first Ctrl+C or SIGTERM stops starting units and gives running ones --cancel-grace to finish; a second one kills them at once; a third raises KeyboardInterrupt.

-s unit:NAME runs one unit without a lock or run results, and never retries it; the process executor uses it.

Usage:

pipeloom run [OPTIONS]

Options:

  --project-dir DIRECTORY      Directory that holds pipeloom.yml.  [default:
                               .]
  --vars TEXT                  Variables as a YAML or JSON mapping; they
                               override the vars block.
  --target TEXT                Target to bind; default_target or the only
                               target when omitted.
  --plugin MODULE:ATTR         A PluginSpec to load besides the installed
                               plugins. Repeatable.
  -s, --select SELECTOR        Models to include: name, tag:x, path:dir,
                               materialized:x, +model, model+, N+model,
                               model+N. Space unions, comma intersects.
                               Repeatable, all are unioned.
  --exclude SELECTOR           Remove the models this selector matches from
                               the selection. Repeatable.
  --state DIR                  Folder of a reference manifest.json (and
                               optionally run_results.json), for the state:
                               and result: selectors. Relative to the project
                               dir unless absolute. `compile --stable` or the
                               artifacts root (target) both work.
  --defer                      Read the parents this run does not select from
                               the relations of the --state manifest instead
                               of this target's, so a dev run of one model
                               reads the production tables. Needs --state.
                               Refused for unit invocations and the task
                               boundary (PLX111).
  --log-format [text|json]     Diagnostics and events on stderr: readable text
                               or one JSON object per line.  [default: text]
  --manifest FILE              Run the plan of this manifest instead of
                               compiling the project.
  --expect-plan-hash HEX       Stop with PLX103 unless the plan hash is this
                               sha256.
  --run-id TEXT                Name of the run. Reusing it continues that run.
                               Default: a timestamp and a suffix.
  --full-refresh BOOLEAN       Rebuild append tables from scratch. Takes an
                               optional true or false.  [default: False]
  --run-started-at ISO8601     Start time of the run, with a UTC offset (for
                               example the start of the orchestrator job).
                               Engines use it to make writes idempotent. Needs
                               --run-id. A reused run id keeps the start it
                               recorded.
  --orchestrator-id KEY=VALUE  An id the orchestrator gave this run, such as
                               job_run_id=42. It goes into the attempt files,
                               the run results and the context of every event.
                               Repeatable; a later duplicate wins. Key:
                               [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}; value: 1 to 256 printable
                               characters.
  --fail-fast                  After the first failure, start no more units.
  --no-lock                    Do not take the run lock.
  --workers INTEGER RANGE      Units to run at once. Default: the target's
                               setting, else min(4, CPUs).  [x>=1]
  --boundary [process|task]    process runs units on threads here; task runs
                               each in its own process. Default: the target's
                               boundary.
  --warn-error                 Exit 1 on warnings too.
  --cancel-grace DURATION      After a stop request (Ctrl+C, SIGTERM) or a
                               timeout, how long running units may finish
                               before they are killed, as 30s, 2m or 30.
                               Default: the setting, else 30s.
  --help                       Show this message and exit.

docs.title: JSON Schema
docs.text:
pipeloom publishes a JSON Schema for each YAML file it reads, so editors can complete keys and flag mistakes before you run anything.

File Schema pipeloom.yml project.json properties files under model_paths properties.json

Models themselves are Python functions, so the @model signature gives completion and type checking in the editor. models.json and defaults.json were removed in 0.9 with YAML model files; the version folders of 0.8 and earlier keep them.

docs.title: Use it in an editor
docs.text:
Put a modeline on the first line of the file. Editors that run the YAML language server (VS Code with the Red Hat YAML extension, for example) pick it up:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://emanuel-luis.github.io/pipeloom/latest/schema/v1/project.json
config_version: 1
name: shop

Use properties.json in properties files.

docs.title: Include plugin options
docs.text:
The published schemas describe the built-in plugins. To get the options of the plugins you have installed, export your own copy and point the modeline at it:

$ pipeloom schema export --out schemas

--plugins builtin limits the export to the built-in plugins. Each plugin's options appear as a branch of the engine, catalog or naming block, selected by kind.

docs.title: Stability and deprecations
docs.text: From 1.0.0 pipeloom follows Semantic Versioning. The decision is in ADR-0016 (amendment 1.0); the artifact schemas are defined in ADR-0049.

docs.title: What you can rely on
docs.text:
Within a major version these do not change in a breaking way:

  • CLI command names, flag names and what they mean, and the exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 130.
  • JSON output that carries a version tag.
  • config_version: 1. It is the only accepted value through 1.x.
  • The artifact schemas pipeloom.manifest/1, pipeloom.run_results/1, pipeloom.event/1, pipeloom.unit_states/1 and pipeloom.unit_graph/1, and the event types.
  • Plugin API 1.0 for plugin authors: the protocols, PluginSpec, the capabilities and pipeloom.testing. A plugin works with a core that has the same major and a minor equal to or above the plugin's; otherwise you get PLU001.
  • The engine conformance kit: the -p pipeloom.testing.pytest_plugin plugin, its --pipeloom-harness option, EngineContract and EngineHarness, and the kit version in the report header. Within 1.x the kit changes only additively: a minor kit version adds cells and optional EngineHarness fields, while a required field, a removed cell or a changed meaning needs a major pipeloom release. Added cells can fail an engine that passed before, so pin pipeloom in CI when a green build must not move.
  • The meaning of each diagnostic code.
  • The documented Python API: the pipeloom top-level exports and pipeloom.api.

Release candidates such as 1.0.0rc1 are published to PyPI, and pip skips them unless you pass --pre. The distributions pin each other with ~= on the prerelease (pipeloom~=1.0.0rc1), which accepts 1.0.0rc1 and the final 1.0.0, but no other minor.

docs.title: What may change in a minor release
docs.text:
• Console text, including messages and hints of diagnostics, log lines and table layout. Read the code or the JSON output instead.
  • Anything undocumented, such as private modules and names that start with an underscore.
  • Additions: new commands, flags, optional fields in artifacts, event types, diagnostic codes and optional plugin members. Readers of artifacts and events should ignore what they do not know.

A rule that let wrong data through can start rejecting configuration in a minor or patch release. The CHANGELOG lists it under Security or Fixed.

docs.title: How a deprecation reaches you
docs.text:
1. The CHANGELOG lists the item under "Deprecated" and the table below gets a row.
  2. When you use the item, pipeloom prints a warning diagnostic with a PLV code. For Python and plugin API members it also raises a Python DeprecationWarning.
  3. The item keeps working for the rest of the major version. It is removed only in the next major, and only after at least one minor release that warned.

docs.title: Experimental features
docs.text:
A feature, flag, config field or artifact field can be marked experimental. It is outside the guarantees above and can change or disappear in any release. You can tell by three marks: the docs say so, the CLI help says so, and the JSON Schema description of the field says so.

  • Using an experimental item prints a warning diagnostic with a PLW code. The run still works.
  • It is promoted to stable or removed within two minor releases after the one that added it. The CHANGELOG says which.
  • Do not depend on an experimental item in a pipeline you cannot edit when it changes.

docs.title: Supported releases
docs.text: Only the latest minor release gets patch releases. Security fixes go to the latest minor. If you run an older minor, upgrade to the latest one to get fixes.

docs.title: Deprecations
docs.text:
Item Deprecated in Replacement Earliest removal

None yet.

docs.title: PLY001
docs.text:
YAML syntax error. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

The file is not valid YAML, holds more than one document, contains a recursive alias, expands an alias above 100000 nodes, or uses an unsupported construct.

docs.title: PLY002
docs.text:
Duplicate key. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A mapping repeats a key. Keys that arrive through a merge key are exempt: explicit keys win.

docs.title: PLY003
docs.text:
Invalid encoding. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

The file is not valid UTF-8 (a UTF-8 BOM is accepted) or has characters YAML forbids.

docs.title: PLY004
docs.text:
File missing or unreadable. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

pipeloom.yml or a properties file does not exist or cannot be read.

docs.title: PLY005
docs.text:
Model module cannot be loaded. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

A Python file under model_paths or model_packages has a syntax error, raised an exception while it was imported, lies outside every python_paths root, or resolves to another file under its module name (an installed package or another module shadows it, or its top-level name is a standard library module). Every such file is reported; the location is the innermost traceback frame in that file, or the syntax error. While any is reported, PLR209 is not, since the missing models may be the ones a properties entry describes.

docs.title: PLS101
docs.text:
Unknown field. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A key is not part of the schema. The message suggests the closest known field.

docs.title: PLS102
docs.text:
Invalid value. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A value has the wrong type or fails a constraint.

docs.title: PLS103
docs.text:
Unsupported config_version. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

config_version is missing or not 1. It is checked first and stops schema validation.

docs.title: PLS104
docs.text:
Literal value in a secret-like field. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A field whose name suggests a secret holds a literal. Use ${secret:...} or ${env:...}.

docs.title: PLS105
docs.text:
Required field missing. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A mapping lacks a required field.

docs.title: PLS106
docs.text:
Unresolved interpolation. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

${env:NAME} is unset with no default, or ${var:name} names an unknown variable.

docs.title: PLS107
docs.text:
Malformed interpolation. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A ${env:...} or ${var:...} expression is malformed.

docs.title: PLS108
docs.text:
Exactly one of several fields required. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

At most one, or exactly one, of a set of fields may be given, for example location or table on a source table.

docs.title: PLR201
docs.text:
Unknown ref. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

An input names a model that does not exist. The hint suggests the closest name.

docs.title: PLR202
docs.text:
Duplicate model name. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

Two models share a name. Names are unique per project.

docs.title: PLR203
docs.text:
Unknown source. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

An input names a source table that no source group in pipeloom.yml declares.

docs.title: PLR204
docs.text:
Unknown target or plugin kind. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

The selected target is not in targets, or an engine, catalog, naming or sink block names a kind that no installed plugin provides.

docs.title: PLR205
docs.text:
Duplicate source. Severity: error. Status: retired. Since: 0.1.

Retired in 0.9: no longer emitted.

Two sources share a name. Names are unique per project.

docs.title: PLR206
docs.text:
model_paths entry does not exist. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A directory listed in model_paths is missing, so no models are read from it.

docs.title: PLR207
docs.text:
No target selected. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

Several targets exist and none was chosen. Use --target, PIPELOOM_TARGET or default_target.

docs.title: PLR208
docs.text:
Unit test reference. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

A unit test in a properties entry gives rows for an alias that is not an input of the model, leaves an input alias without rows, or reuses a case name of its model.

docs.title: PLR209
docs.text:
Properties entry names no model, or describes one twice. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

An entry of a properties file names a model that does not exist, or a model that another properties entry already describes. Each model has at most one properties entry. The hint suggests the closest model name, or points at the first entry.

docs.title: PLR210
docs.text:
Input name matches a table in several source groups. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

A parameter of a Python model binds by name to a source table, and tables with that name exist in more than one source group. Bind it explicitly with inputs={'name': source('group', 'table')}.

docs.title: PLG301
docs.text:
Cycle in the graph. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

Models depend on each other in a loop. The message lists the path.

docs.title: PLG302
docs.text:
Self-reference. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A model lists itself among its own inputs.

docs.title: PLG303
docs.text:
Selector matched nothing. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A selector atom matched no model. This is a warning, not an error.

docs.title: PLG304
docs.text:
Unknown selector method. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A selector uses a method other than name, tag, path, materialized, unit, state or result. Exit code 2.

docs.title: PLG305
docs.text:
Malformed selector. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A selector cannot be parsed, for example an empty atom or a depth of 0. Exit code 2.

docs.title: PLG306
docs.text:
Unknown unit. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

A unit: selector names a unit that the project does not have. Ephemeral models are not units.

docs.title: PLG307
docs.text:
State selector without reference. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.8.

A state: or result: selector atom was used without --state. Point --state at a folder that holds the reference manifest.json. Exit code 2.

docs.title: PLG308
docs.text:
No run results in the reference. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.8.

A result: selector atom needs the reference's run_results.json, and the --state folder has none. Exit code 2.

docs.title: PLP401
docs.text:
merge or scd2 without unique_key. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A model writes with merge or scd2 but sets no write.unique_key.

docs.title: PLP402
docs.text:
incremental without column. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A model is materialized as incremental but sets no incremental.column to compare with the watermark.

docs.title: PLP403
docs.text:
Aggregate expectation with drop. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

An aggregate check (unique, row_count, freshness) cannot drop rows. Use warn or fail.

docs.title: PLP404
docs.text:
incremental.input not in inputs. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

incremental.input names an alias that is not one of the model's inputs.

docs.title: PLP405
docs.text:
Write option not applied by this strategy. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A declared write option would be ignored: unique_key, update_condition or deletes with a strategy that does not use them, tracked_columns outside scd2, write on an ephemeral model, or incremental on a model that is not incremental.

docs.title: PLP406
docs.text:
Ephemeral fan-out above threshold. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

An ephemeral model is inlined in more units than ephemeral_fanout_warn. Make it an intermediate to compute it once.

docs.title: PLP407
docs.text:
replace_partitions without partition_by. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

The replace_partitions strategy needs partition_by to know which partitions to replace.

docs.title: PLP408
docs.text:
Ephemeral model with no consumer. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

No persisted model reads this ephemeral model, directly or through other ephemeral models, so it never runs.

docs.title: PLP409
docs.text:
View inlines an ephemeral model. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

A view cannot read an ephemeral model, because its query is stored in the catalog and an ephemeral model has no relation to name. A view is a model function that returns ctx.sql(...).

docs.title: PLP410
docs.text:
append with lookback reloads rows. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

An incremental model appends with a lookback above zero, so rows inside the window are written again. Use merge with a unique_key.

docs.title: PLP411
docs.text:
Expectations on a view or ephemeral model. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

A view or an ephemeral model writes no rows of its own, so it cannot carry expectations. Put them on a table that reads it.

docs.title: PLP412
docs.text:
Quarantine relation collides with a model. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

A model's quarantine table is named __quarantine, and another model already has that name in the same catalog and schema.

docs.title: PLP413
docs.text:
Intermediate model with a write option. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

An intermediate model is rewritten whole at a location of its own. It cannot be incremental, use a strategy other than overwrite, or set partition_by.

docs.title: PLP414
docs.text:
Contract on a view or ephemeral model. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

A view or an ephemeral model writes no batch of its own, so its columns cannot be checked. Put the contract on a table that reads it.

docs.title: PLP415
docs.text:
Data tests that cannot run. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

data_tests is set on an ephemeral model, which writes no table to test, or a relationships check names as its parent the model itself, a descendant, an ephemeral model, an intermediate model (an intermediate table is not there when its model is not built in the run), or a model that closes a cycle among input and relationship edges. Test the relationship on a table that is not upstream of its parent.

docs.title: PLP416
docs.text:
scd2 options conflict. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

A model writing with scd2 sets an option the strategy cannot apply: an empty tracked_columns, a tracked column that is part of unique_key, deletes with mode: soft, or a unique_key, tracked_columns, partition_by, cluster_by, deletes.column or contract column named valid_from, valid_to or is_current (scd2 adds those columns itself).

docs.title: PLC501
docs.text:
Strategy unsupported by engine. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

The write strategy is not in the selected engine's capabilities.

docs.title: PLC502
docs.text:
SQL model on an engine without SQL. Severity: error. Status: retired. Since: 0.1.

Retired in 0.9: no longer emitted.

A SQL model targets an engine that cannot run SQL.

docs.title: PLC503
docs.text:
boundary task with a non-shared state store. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

Units run as separate tasks, but the state store is local to one process or machine.

docs.title: PLC504
docs.text:
Catalog incompatible with engine. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

The catalog plugin does not list the selected engine in its compatible engines.

docs.title: PLC505
docs.text:
Non-idempotent append with retries. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

An append model retries on an engine without idempotent writes, which could write the same rows twice.

docs.title: PLC506
docs.text:
Source format unsupported. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A source declares a format the selected engine cannot read.

docs.title: PLC507
docs.text:
View without views support. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A model is materialized as a view on an engine without catalog views.

docs.title: PLC508
docs.text:
frame_api narwhals without portable engine. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A Python model asks for Narwhals frames on an engine whose frames are not portable.

docs.title: PLC509
docs.text:
Materialization unsupported by engine. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

The materialization is not in the selected engine's capabilities.

docs.title: PLC510
docs.text:
Expectations on an engine without quality. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

The selected engine does not declare the quality capability, so it cannot evaluate expectations or data tests, or count nulls in non-nullable contract columns.

docs.title: PLC513
docs.text:
SQL translation needs the sqlglot extra. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

The model's sql_dialect differs from the dialect of the target engine, so its ctx.sql queries must be translated, and sqlglot is not installed. Install pipeloom[sqlglot], or remove sql_dialect and write the queries in the engine's dialect.

docs.title: PLK601
docs.text:
Callable file or function not found. Severity: error. Status: retired. Since: 0.1.

Retired in 0.9: no longer emitted.

The Python module is not under python_paths, cannot be parsed, or does not define the function.

docs.title: PLK602
docs.text:
Callable parameters do not match inputs. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

Inputs are passed by keyword, so a model function cannot take *args or positional-only parameters, and every inputs= key must name a parameter (any key is accepted with **kwargs).

docs.title: PLK603
docs.text:
SQL references undeclared table. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

A model's SQL reads a table that is neither an input alias nor a CTE. Checked only when sqlglot is installed (extra: sqlglot).

docs.title: PLK604
docs.text:
Name bound at module level by something other than a def. Severity: warning. Status: retired. Since: 0.1.

Retired in 0.9: no longer emitted.

The callable's name is bound by an assignment, import or class, so its parameters cannot be checked.

docs.title: PLK605
docs.text:
SQL not parseable. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

sqlglot could not parse the model's SQL, so its tables were not checked. Checked only when sqlglot is installed.

docs.title: PLK606
docs.text:
ctx.sql on an engine without SQL. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

The model function calls ctx.sql, but the target engine runs no SQL (its sql_dialect is None), so the call raises at run time (PLX101). Write the model with frames, or choose an engine with SQL.

docs.title: PLF701
docs.text:
Engine unreachable. Severity: error. Status: reserved. Since: 0.2.

Reserved: not emitted yet.

docs.title: PLF702
docs.text:
Source missing. Severity: error. Status: reserved. Since: 0.2.

Reserved: not emitted yet.

docs.title: PLF703
docs.text:
Target schema drift detected. Severity: error. Status: reserved. Since: 0.2.

Reserved: not emitted yet.

docs.title: PLU001
docs.text:
Plugin API mismatch. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A plugin was built for another plugin API version. The major version must match and the plugin's minor must not be above the core's.

docs.title: PLU002
docs.text:
Duplicate plugin kind. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

Two installed plugins provide the same kind in one group, and a config names it.

docs.title: PLU003
docs.text:
Plugin failed to load. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

A plugin module cannot be imported, does not resolve to a PluginSpec, or its group or kind differs from the entry point that registered it.

docs.title: PLU004
docs.text:
Demo engine not installed. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 1.1.

pipeloom demo runs on the DuckDB engine and found no duckdb engine plugin. The message lists the engine plugins that are installed, and the hint is the install command. The demo never falls back to another engine. Exit code 1.

docs.title: PLE401
docs.text:
Sink disabled. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.1.

An event sink failed failure_budget times in a row and was disabled. The other sinks keep receiving events and get a sink.disabled event.

docs.title: PLM201
docs.text:
Write failed. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

The engine failed to write a model's result or to create its view.

docs.title: PLM202
docs.text:
Schema change rejected. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

The batch schema differs from the existing target and the model's on_schema_change policy does not allow it.

docs.title: PLM203
docs.text:
Watermark CAS conflict. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

The stored watermark changed while the unit ran, so the new one was not saved. The data was already written. Another run on the same target is the usual cause.

docs.title: PLM204
docs.text:
Input read failed. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

An input of a model could not be read from its source or from the catalog.

docs.title: PLM205
docs.text:
Incremental watermark unusable. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

The incremental column is missing from the input, its type differs from the stored watermark, or a lookback is set on a column that is not a timestamp or date.

docs.title: PLM206
docs.text:
Write key invalid. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

A unique_key or partition_by column is missing from the batch, or a merge batch repeats a unique_key.

docs.title: PLM207
docs.text:
Write refused by the idempotency guard. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.4.

The engine skipped the write because this model already has a later transaction version: a newer run, an overlapping run started with --no-lock, or a host clock that ran behind. The engine refuses before it changes any data. Wait for the other run, check the clocks, or turn the guard off in the engine options.

docs.title: PLM208
docs.text:
Model contract violated. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

The model output does not match its declared columns: a column is missing or extra, a logical type differs from the declared dtype, or a column with nullable: false holds a null (NaN counts as null). The check runs after the expectations and before the schema policy, the quarantine write and the table write, so nothing is written. Permanent.

docs.title: PLQ301
docs.text:
Expectation failed. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

An expectation with on_violation: fail found violating rows, or the share of dropped rows exceeded quality.max_drop_ratio. The unit fails before writing; the counts are still recorded in run_results.

docs.title: PLQ302
docs.text:
Expectation references an unknown column. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

An expectation names a column the model output lacks, or its expr cannot be evaluated by the engine.

docs.title: PLQ303
docs.text:
Data test failed. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

A data test with on_violation: fail found violations in the written table: nulls, duplicate keys, or child keys with no parent row. Data tests run after the write and the watermark commit, so the data stays written; the unit fails, its descendants are skipped and the run exits 1. Permanent: only retry_on: any retries it.

docs.title: PLX101
docs.text:
Model raised. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

A model's body raised, or returned a value its engine cannot use as a relation.

docs.title: PLX102
docs.text:
Timeout. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

A unit attempt ran longer than its timeout. A timed-out unit is not retried and its descendants are skipped.

docs.title: PLX103
docs.text:
Plan hash mismatch. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

The plan hash of the manifest or of the compiled project differs from --expect-plan-hash.

docs.title: PLX104
docs.text:
Cancelled. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.3.

A unit was still running when the run was stopped and did not finish within the grace period, or the stop was hard. The run ends cancelled with exit code 130.

docs.title: PLX105
docs.text:
Run lock held. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

Another run holds the lock of this project and target. The message names the holder, its run and when its lease expires.

docs.title: PLX106
docs.text:
Unit process exited without a result. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

A unit started under boundary task exited without writing its attempt file. The excerpt holds the last lines of its log.

docs.title: PLX107
docs.text:
Manifest invalid. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.2.

The manifest cannot be read, has another schema, was edited after it was written, or belongs to another project or target.

docs.title: PLX108
docs.text:
Run start time conflict. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.4.

--run-started-at differs from the start the run recorded when it first ran. A reused run id keeps its recorded start. Exit code 2.

docs.title: PLX109
docs.text:
Secret reference not resolved. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

A ${secret:provider/path} reference in a plugin's options could not be resolved when the command executed: the provider is unknown or failed, the resolved options are invalid, or the plugin could not be built with them. The message names the provider and path, never a value.

docs.title: PLX110
docs.text:
Reference state unusable. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.8.

The --state folder cannot serve as a reference: it is missing, its manifest.json is unreadable or belongs to another project, or its run_results.json is unreadable, has another schema or belongs to another project. Compile again with --stable to write a fresh reference.

docs.title: PLX111
docs.text:
Defer refused. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.8.

--defer cannot be used here: the invocation is a unit invocation, the boundary is task (children rerun units without the reference), or the reference was compiled for another catalog kind. Use --boundary process, or build the parents here. Exit code 2.

docs.title: PLX112
docs.text:
Parent not deferred. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.8.

With --defer, an unselected parent is read from this target instead of the reference: it is an intermediate model, it is missing from the reference, or the reference has no relation for it.

docs.title: PLX113
docs.text:
Run cannot be retried. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.8.

pipeloom retry --from names a run that cannot be retried: its folder or run_results.json is missing (it never existed, never finished or is still running), it belongs to another project, or it ran another target. Retry with the target of that run.

docs.title: PLX114
docs.text:
Unit test failed. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

pipeloom test ran the model body on the given rows and the output differs from expect. The message lists up to 10 missing and 10 unexpected rows; the unit_test.failed event holds up to 50 of each. Rows compare as a multiset over the expect columns.

docs.title: PLX115
docs.text:
Unit test cannot run. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

A unit test could not run: a CSV file is missing or unreadable, a value does not cast to its column type, a column holds only nulls and declares no type, the model body raised, or the engine lacks from_rows or to_rows (plugin API 0.5). Declare columns on the given, or upgrade the engine plugin.

docs.title: PLX117
docs.text:
State store cannot list runs. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

pipeloom runs needs StateStore.list_runs (plugin API 0.5), and the configured state store does not provide it. Use --artifacts to read the run results under the artifacts root instead, or upgrade the store plugin.

docs.title: PLX118
docs.text:
Run not found. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

pipeloom runs show, or runs ls --before, names a run id that the state store (or, with --artifacts, the artifacts root) does not hold for this project and target. Check the target, or list the runs with pipeloom runs ls.

docs.title: PLX120
docs.text:
View model did not return ctx.sql(...), or passed it inputs=. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

A Python view model runs in view mode: its input parameters are placeholders that only ctx.sql may name, and ctx.sql returns the query the catalog stores. The function returned something else, passed inputs= frames to ctx.sql, or used an input as a frame.

docs.title: PLX121
docs.text:
DuckDB extension not installed. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 1.1.

The DuckDB engine needs an extension (delta for a Delta source, or one listed in the engine's extensions option) that is not installed in its extension_directory, and install_extensions is off, so nothing is downloaded. The code appears in the message of the error that the read or write reports (PLM204, PLM201 or PLX101). Preinstall the extension into that directory on a machine with network access, or turn install_extensions on.

docs.title: PLX122
docs.text:
Order-dependent operation on a lazy frame. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 1.1.

A Python model with frame_api narwhals used an operation that needs a row order (cum_sum, shift, diff, first or last) on a lazy frame (DuckDB, Spark or polars lazy), which has none. Give the expression an explicit order with .over(order_by=...), or sort first; see the portable models guide.

docs.title: PLA001
docs.text:
Unsupported execution mode. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.6.

The Airflow plugin was configured with an execution mode it does not support. DOCKER is not supported in 0.6; use local, virtualenv, kubernetes, databricks or watcher.

docs.title: PLA002
docs.text:
Invalid Airflow plugin configuration. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.6.

A configuration of the Airflow plugin cannot be used: the manifest load method without a manifest path, a relative path, a virtualenv mode without a directory, a kubernetes mode without an image, a pod_kwargs or operator_args key that pipeloom sets itself, an unknown asset_uri placeholder, a WATCHER setting out of range or a WATCHER selection made only of unit: selectors, or a full_refresh param that is not a boolean.

docs.title: PLA003
docs.text:
Selection renders no units. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.6.

The DAG's select and exclude selectors match no unit of the plan, so the DAG would hold no unit task.

docs.title: PLA004
docs.text:
Unit task ended without a visible unit result. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.6.

An Airflow task ended without an attempt file for its unit under artifacts.root. When the task succeeded, the root is not shared between the workers and the finalize task. The unit is recorded as failed, so the run fails.

docs.title: PLA005
docs.text:
Unsupported Airflow version. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.6.

The plugin supports Airflow 3.2 up to, not including, 4.0.

docs.title: PLA006
docs.text:
PROJECT compile cache unusable. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.6.

The directory that holds the compile cache of the project load method cannot be read or written. The project compiles on every DAG parse until it is fixed.

docs.title: PLA007
docs.text:
Target boundary is not task. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.6.

Each unit runs in its own process, so the target should set boundary: task. Then PLC503 checks that the state store is shared between workers.

docs.title: PLA008
docs.text:
WATCHER artifacts root not resolved. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

In WATCHER mode the DAG reads the artifacts root from pipeloom.yml at parse time, so the watchers can read the attempt files. The file could not be read, or its artifacts.root holds a ${...} reference; set execution.watcher_artifacts_root to the absolute path. At run time, the producer's run left no run_results.json under that root: the root differs from the one the run writes to.

docs.title: PLA009
docs.text:
WATCHER producer ended without run results. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.9.

The producer task of a WATCHER DAG ended, but neither an attempt file of the unit nor run_results.json appeared under the artifacts root within the grace period. The producer was killed or failed before it ran the unit. The watcher fails, and a retry of the watcher runs the unit itself.

docs.title: PLD001
docs.text:
Task limit exceeded. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

A Databricks job would hold more than 1,000 tasks, its finalize task included. Set task_grouping in the deploy block, or split the project into pipelines.

docs.title: PLD002
docs.text:
Submit task limit (never emitted, PLD001 covers it). Severity: error. Status: reserved. Since: 0.4.

Reserved: not emitted yet.

docs.title: PLD003
docs.text:
Task groups form a cycle. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

With task_grouping set, the units of one group depend on units of another group in both directions, so the grouped tasks cannot be ordered. Group by another key or turn grouping off.

docs.title: PLD004
docs.text:
Invalid Databricks deploy options for this plan or target. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

The deploy block cannot be rendered: an unknown pipeline or compute key, environment_version 1, more than 10 serverless environments in a job, a key in settings that pipeloom owns, a ${secret:...} reference, an artifacts root that is unset or relative, a state store that is not shared, a group that spans two computes, or an ephemeral run on a job cluster.

docs.title: PLD005
docs.text:
Compute rule matches no model. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

No model of the plan matches the select selectors of a compute rule, so the rule never applies.

docs.title: PLD006
docs.text:
More than one job carries the pipeloom_job tag. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

Two or more Databricks jobs hold the same pipeloom_job tag, so deploy cannot tell which one it owns. Delete or untag the extra jobs; the message lists their ids.

docs.title: PLD007
docs.text:
Job or run not found. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

No Databricks job carries the pipeloom_job tag of this pipeline, or the run asked for does not exist. Deploy the job first, or pass --ensure to run so it deploys one; check the run id and the pipeline.

docs.title: PLD008
docs.text:
Deployed job is out of date. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

The job in the workspace was deployed from other settings than the project renders now (its pipeloom_settings_hash tag differs). Deploy again, or pass --ensure to run so it deploys first.

docs.title: PLD009
docs.text:
Databricks API request failed. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

A call to the Databricks REST API returned an error. The message carries the HTTP status, the error code and the message of the API, with registered secret values masked. Check the connection, the permissions of the caller and the workspace path.

docs.title: PLD010
docs.text:
No Databricks connection configured. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

The command needs a workspace and none is configured. Pass --profile, set DATABRICKS_CONFIG_PROFILE, set DATABRICKS_HOST with its credentials, or run on a Databricks runtime. pipeloom never picks a profile by itself.

docs.title: PLD011
docs.text:
Task ended without a unit result. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

A Databricks task failed before its unit wrote an attempt file, for example because the cluster was lost, so the unit has no result of its own. Finalize records the unit as failed with the termination message of the task. Read the task's log on the run page; repair reruns it.

docs.title: PLD012
docs.text:
Project file cannot be uploaded. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

A project file is above 10 MB, is a notebook (a Databricks notebook header or an .ipynb file), is unreadable or lies outside the project folder, so it cannot be stored as a plain workspace file.

docs.title: PLD013
docs.text:
Dynamic value reference not resolved in a task parameter. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

A parameter of a Databricks task still holds a {{...}} reference, so the platform did not substitute it. The task stops before it runs anything. Check the job's parameters and the Databricks runtime that runs the task.

docs.title: PLD014
docs.text:
Run is still active. Severity: error. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

A repair was asked for a Databricks job run that has not ended. Wait for it to finish or cancel it, then repair.

docs.title: PLD015
docs.text:
Selection covers part of a task group. Severity: warning. Status: active. Since: 0.5.

With task_grouping set, a task runs every unit of its group, so a selection that names only some of them still runs the whole group. Select the whole group, or turn grouping off, to run exactly the units chosen.
